list.shortDescription: A Levantine sesame cookie with pistachio pieces, associated with Damascus’s Al-Midan neighborhood during Ottoman rule and now sold across the broader Arab world.

cover.altText: Barazek, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Monegasque appetizer fritter filled with Swiss chard, rice and ricotta; other fillings include pumpkin, minced meat, leeks or eggs. In Monaco it is especially eaten on 19 November.

cover.altText: Barbajuan: Grande raviolo chiamato barbagiuai nella zona di Ventimiglia, Liguria, Italia

list.shortDescription: A Swiss hard spice biscuit from Basel, made with honey, hazelnuts, almonds, candied peel, and Kirsch. Baked in a thin layer, it is glazed with sugar while hot and cut into rectangular pieces.

cover.altText: Basler Läckerli: Basler Läckerli, a typical swiss bakery from Basle

list.shortDescription: A Spanish crustless cheesecake created in 1988 at La Viña in San Sebastián, with a caramelized surface and creamy, custard-like interior from high-temperature baking.

cover.altText: Basque-style cheesecake: Чизкейк Сан-Себастьян в кафе в Стамбуле

list.shortDescription: A warm German potato dish of fried potatoes, eggs, green onions, parsley, and bacon or ham, mixed in a pan and fried as an omelette. Eaten for breakfast, lunch, or dinner.

cover.altText: Bauernfrühstück: Bauernfrühstück, here with fried potatoes, scrambled eggs, smoked meat and onions, with pickles and garnish

list.shortDescription: In Bavarian cuisine, shredded cabbage is simmered in beef stock with pork lard, onion and apple, then seasoned with salt, black pepper, caraway, sugar and vinegar. It is served alongside bratwurst or roast pork.

cover.altText: Bayrisch Kraut: Speckknödel auf Bayrisch Kraut

list.shortDescription: A baked dish pairing beef fillet with duxelles inside puff pastry. Prosciutto or dry-cured ham may wrap the contents to retain moisture and keep the pastry from becoming soggy; the beef may also be coated with mustard.

cover.altText: Beef Wellington: Beef Wellington created by Chefs Samuel & Kathleen, 2019

list.shortDescription: A Belgian waffle with a light batter, large squares, and deep pockets, leavened with yeast or baking powder. It is eaten at breakfast or as a dessert with cream, fruit, chocolate, syrup, butter, or ice cream.

cover.altText: Belgian waffle, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A sweet oval cake from Modena made with flour, milk, eggs, butter, and honey, later sugar. It may be filled with jam or savòr, then sliced and soaked in Lambrusco before eating.

cover.altText: Bensone: Bensone, balsone o balsòn: dolce semplice tipico del modenese, composto da farina, uova, burro, zucchero e lievito

list.shortDescription: A German jam doughnut without a central hole, made from sweet yeast dough fried in lard or cooking oil, filled with jam, and coated in powdered sugar or glaze.

cover.altText: Berliner, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: Filipino barbecue consists of marinated pork, chicken, and offal skewers grilled and served as street food in the Philippines, a tradition dating to the 1950s.

cover.altText: Betamax (food): Very known street food in the Philippines popular as a night snack

list.shortDescription: A vegetable dish of the Indian subcontinent made with okra slit and stuffed with garam masala and other local ground spices, then stir-fried or sautéed. It accompanies steamed rice and dal or chapati.

cover.altText: Bhendi fry: Indianfood, Indian curry

list.shortDescription: A French sweet dessert of milk or cream and sugar, thickened with rice flour, gelatin or cornflour, often flavored with almonds, then set in a mould and served cold.

cover.altText: Biancomangiare PAT, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A traditional Sri Lankan coconut cake made with shredded coconut, jaggery, semolina, and spices. Its dark, moist crumb is enjoyed during festive and religious occasions, including Christmas, New Year’s Eve, and Sinhala and Tamil New Year.

cover.altText: Bibikkan: Slices of fresh Bibikkan

list.shortDescription: A Japanese snack made from shredded fish surimi in the style of a breaded cutlet. The original Big Katsu from Kadō was introduced in 1987; varieties are sold at convenience and snack stores.

cover.altText: Big Katsu, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A U.S. cinnamon-flavored chewing gum introduced by the William Wrigley Jr. Company in 1975, popular as a souvenir for visitors from Ireland and the United Kingdom.

cover.altText: Big Red: Kaneltyggegummi Wrigley Big Red Cinnamon Gum

list.shortDescription: An Indonesian sweetmeat made with tapioca flour, eggs, sugar, yeast, and coconut milk, commonly flavored with kaffir lime or pandan and also sold in banana, durian, cheese, and chocolate varieties.

cover.altText: Bika Ambon: Bika Ambon from Medan

list.shortDescription: An Ifugao steamed rice cake of pounded glutinous rice wrapped in banana or rattan leaves. Variants add sesame seeds or sweet potato; uncooked binakle and rice wine are offered to bulul ancestor spirits in Ifugao rites.
An Italian sweet, leavened bread from Lombardy’s Valtellina Valley, typically prepared for Christmas and essential to the festivities.

cover.altText: Bisciola PAT: food tipical of valtellina

list.shortDescription: A Bulgarian no-bake tea cake made with digestive biscuits and optional chocolate glaze, resembling an American icebox cake.

cover.altText: Biscuit cake: Food by Ms Ujwala Kasambe

list.shortDescription: A traditional Bangladeshi yoghurt dessert from Bogra, made as a variation of mishti doi and enjoyed throughout the country.

cover.altText: Bogurar doi: Dahi of Bogura

list.shortDescription: A Portuguese flatbread from Madeira and Porto Santo, shaped like a cake and cooked on a flat basalt slab, served with garlic butter or filled with octopus, espetada, milho frito, or steak.

cover.altText: Bolo do caco: Bolo do caco is a typical flatbread from the island of Madeira (Portugal)

list.shortDescription: An Indonesian steamed sponge cupcake made with wheat flour, sugar, eggs, milk, and soda, often flavored with vanilla, chocolate, pandan, or strawberry essence.

cover.altText: Bolu kukus: Kue bolu kukus, Pasar Bulu Semarang

list.shortDescription: An Indian confection made from fried chickpea flour, served either as a savoury snack or sweetened as a dessert.

cover.altText: Boondi: Boondi Mithai, A Common Andhra Indian Festival Sweet Snack

list.shortDescription: A Filipino offal dish of pork or beef lungs and heart sautéed with tomatoes, chilies, onions, garlic, and pepper until crisp, served with rice or alcoholic beverages.

cover.altText: Bopis: Bopis is made from ground pig's lungs and liver with water spinach, carrots, and spices

list.shortDescription: An Iranian salad with spinach-and-yogurt and ancient Persian eggplant versions. The Urfa version uses lamb and vegetarian meatballs; borani also appears in Turkish cuisine and is popular in the Caucasus and Afghanistan.

cover.altText: Borani: Bouranee, an Iranian side dish, made from yogurt and spinach

list.shortDescription: A traditional feast dish of the Kanak people in New Caledonia, named from the Drehu word puhnya, meaning “bundle” or “pack.” It is also eaten in Vanuatu as bunya or bunia.

cover.altText: Bougna, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A South African toasted sandwich of bread, cheese, tomato, and onion, associated with braai culture and prepared over an open fire.

cover.altText: Braaibroodjie: Braai broodjies are sandwiches cooked on an open fire

list.shortDescription: A Tunisian pastry of semolina-based dough folded around a savoury filling and fried or baked, commonly served as an appetizer or during Ramadan.
A Belgian waffle cooked between two patterned plates, with regional varieties shaped by different irons and recipes. It may be made fresh or heated after commercial baking and packaging.

cover.altText: Brussels waffle, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: An Italian hazelnut- or almond-flavoured biscuit made with egg-white-and-sugar meringue and roasted chopped nuts, crunchy outside and soft within. Produced in Prato, Tuscany, it is also known as mandorlati di San Clemente.

cover.altText: Brutti e buoni: Brutti ma buoni - biscuits italiens

list.shortDescription: A Slovak national dish pairing halušky with bryndza, optionally sprinkled with cooked smoked pork fat or bacon and chives or spring onions.

cover.altText: Bryndzové halušky: Bryndzové halušky so slaninou

list.shortDescription: A fine powder of roasted barley and legumes, typical of Tunisian cuisine and served as either a paste or drink. Consumed throughout North Africa since Pharos times, it was carried by travellers and nomads for its nutritional value and ease of transport.

cover.altText: Bssisa: Made of grilled wheat, olive oil, accompanied with dried fruits

list.shortDescription: A Malaysian dessert and breakfast of pearled sago, sweet potatoes, yams, bananas, pandan leaves, sugar, salt, and coconut milk, served hot or cold.

cover.altText: Bubur cha cha: ​摩摩喳喳

list.shortDescription: An Indonesian black rice pudding made by boiling glutinous rice until soft, then adding coconut milk and palm or cane sugar. It is served as a dessert, snack, or breakfast.

cover.altText: Bubur ketan hitam: Bubur injin is Balinese version of bubur ketan hitam, or sweet black rice pudding served with coconut milk. Served as a breakfast in Gayatri Bungalows, Ubud, Bali, Indonesia

list.shortDescription: A Sicilian circular cake filled with figs and nuts, traditionally associated with Christmas. It is distinct from the similar Lucchese buccellato di Lucca.

cover.altText: Buccellato PAT: Buccellato, a Sicilian circular cake

list.shortDescription: A Chinese vegetarian dish of various vegetables and other vegetarian ingredients, sometimes seafood or eggs, cooked in a soy sauce-based liquid with seasonings until tender. It is traditionally enjoyed by Buddhist monks.

cover.altText: Buddha's delight, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Hanoi dish of grilled fatty pork served over white rice noodles with herbs and a dipping sauce. It was described by Vietnamese food writer Vũ Bằng in 1959.

cover.altText: Bun cha: bun cha hanoi Vietnamese Bún chả food

list.shortDescription: An Indonesian-Javanese dish of grated coconut meat, anchovies and spices, wrapped in papaya, cassava, or taro leaves and boiled in coconut milk with spices. A Java favourite sold at street stalls during Ramadhan.

cover.altText: Buntil: Buntil, Javanese traditional food made of papaya leaves which is wraps grated coconut and anchovies and boiled in coconut milk

list.shortDescription: An Indonesian folded rice pancake served in whitish coconut milk-based soup flavored with fish and topped with fried shallots. A Palembang specialty popular for breakfast.

cover.altText: Burgo, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Ligurian Italian seafood soup or stew, sometimes slow-cooked and sometimes prepared quickly, with a texture similar to a stew.

cover.altText: Buridda: Buridda di seppie e piselli, un tipico piatto ligure

list.shortDescription: A Myanmar fried rice made with paw hsan hmwe, a fragrant short-grain rice, and commonly boiled peas, onions, garlic, and dark soy sauce. It is a breakfast dish, sometimes topped with a fried egg.
A veal-based cotoletta from Bologna, Italy, also called petroniana after Petronius, the fifth-century bishop and patron saint of the city.

cover.altText: Cotoletta alla bolognese: Italian food - tipycal steak from Bologna

list.shortDescription: A fish stew from Brittany made with oily fish such as herring, sprats, and mackerel, plus potatoes, onions, and garlic, traditionally served over a toasted baguette.

cover.altText: Cotriade: Cotriade bretonne

list.shortDescription: A traditional American dessert of plain, dense butter cake served with sweet sauce, glaze, or custard poured over it. The glaze is cornstarch-based and may be flavored with sugar, vanilla, chocolate, butterscotch, lemon, or strawberry.

cover.altText: Cottage Pudding: Cottage pudding in a 1930s magazine flavored with spices and molasses, served with a raisin sauce

list.shortDescription: A West Coast American salad featuring crab meat, dating to the early 1900s and also known as the King of Salads.

cover.altText: Crab Louie: Crab Louie salad at Princess Seafood Restaurant

list.shortDescription: A Chaozhou dish of small, deep-fried crab cakes shaped like jujube fruit, made with crab meat, pork fat, water chestnuts, eggs, vegetables, and herbs. The mixture is wrapped in tofu skin, rolled, and cut into bite-sized pieces; in Thailand, it is popular among Thai Chinese people as hoicho.

cover.altText: Crab jujube, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Belgian brioche filled with nib sugar flavoured with orange, lemon, vanilla, or almond essence. The sugar melts during baking and cools into sugar-encrusted gaps beneath a viennoiserie dough overlay.
A Louisiana pasta dish made with crawfish tail meat, onion, garlic, Creole seasoning, cream, wine, salt, pepper, and butter. Created by chef Pierre Hilzim and named for his wife, Monica Davidson.

cover.altText: Crawfish Monica: Bowl of Crawfish Monica and cup of Abita beer, at free Wednesday concert in Lafayette Square, New Orleans

list.shortDescription: A Japanese sweet bread from Kōriyama, Fukushima, made with thick-sliced bread coated in milk-flavored cream and sold in original, fruit, and coffee variations.

cover.altText: Cream Box: Cleambox

list.shortDescription: A Maryland Eastern Shore soup made with lump blue crab meat, onion, whole milk or half-and-half, butter, and flour or cornstarch, seasoned chiefly with Old Bay.

cover.altText: Cream of crab soup: Maryland cream of crab soup at Liberty Road Seafood Restaurant in Liberty, MD

list.shortDescription: An Italian marzipan sweet from Caltanissetta, Sicily, named for the nearby Church of Santa Croce and once made by Benedictine sisters for the feast of the Most Holy Crucifix; forgotten after 1908, it has recently been rediscovered.

cover.altText: Crocetta of Caltanissetta, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: Small, square, flat pasta from Savoie in southeastern France, traditionally made at home with buckwheat, wheat, or both, and used mainly for croziflette and crozets with diots.

cover.altText: Crozets de Savoie: crozets de Savoie

list.shortDescription: Cuajada is a dairy product traditionally made from sheep’s milk, though now more often produced industrially from cow’s milk. It is popular in northern Spain, Colombia, Venezuela and parts of Central America.

cover.altText: Cuajada: Cuajada

list.shortDescription: A Sicilian porridge of boiled wheatberries and sugar, eaten on December 13 for Saint Lucy’s feast. It commemorates Sicily’s relief from a food shortage and the arrival of wheat in Palermo in 1646.

cover.altText: Cuccìa PAT: Cuccìa, piatto tipico lucano

list.shortDescription: An Italian dessert of honey, dissolved sugar, and diced almonds, eaten at Christmas in Calabria, Campania, Apulia, and Sicily, but prepared year-round in Ponente Ligure.

cover.altText: Cupeta: Croccante

list.shortDescription: Curd rice, also called yogurt rice, is an Indian dish made with plain unsweetened yogurt. It is most popular in Tamil Nadu, Kerala, Karnataka, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Rajasthan, Gujarat, and Maharashtra.

cover.altText: Curd rice: Curd rice with puppads and cashews

list.shortDescription: A tall, multilayered sandwich of assorted meats, cheeses, and condiments, named for Dagwood Bumstead of Blondie. Scripter Dean Young said his father, Chic Young, began drawing huge sandwiches in the strip in 1936.
An Odia dish of yogurt and eggplant, prepared especially for festivals and sometimes made without onion or garlic when those ingredients are prohibited.

cover.altText: Dahi baigana, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Cretan salad of soaked paximadi bread topped with tomatoes and feta or mizithra, seasoned with dried oregano, with olives, capers, and caper berries often added.

cover.altText: Dakos, a photograph of the dish

cover.altText: Dal Tadka: 3 lentils with transparent background

list.shortDescription: A South Asian meal of thick lentil soup, dal, paired with cooked rice, bhat. A daily staple in South Asia and the Caribbean, providing protein and carbohydrates.
A Batak dish of water buffalo milk from Tapanuli, North Sumatra. It is a mainstay of the Batak diet and is traded in Tapanuli’s onan markets.

cover.altText: Dali ni Horbo: DALI NI HORBO, Batak's traditional 'cheese' cuisine

list.shortDescription: A South Asian puri made from whole-wheat flour, deep-fried and filled with chickpea or lentil dal. Caribbean and Mauritian variants use white flour, are griddle-baked on a tava, and commonly contain split peas.

cover.altText: Dalpuri: Even in times of simplicity, nothing can compare to the complex blends of flavor in Bengali cuisine. Daalpuris are a common Bengali street food usually enjoyed with a side of green chutney

cover.altText: Dame blanche, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Taiwanese breakfast of thin dough kneaded from flour, potato starch, glutinous rice flour, and water, topped with a baked omelet. Regional recipes vary, and it is sold at breakfast shops, restaurants, night markets, and supermarkets.

cover.altText: Danbing: the-cooking-of-joy.blogspot.com/2014/03/dan-bing-taiwanes

list.shortDescription: A Tausug Filipino dessert of crêpes made with ground glutinous rice and coconut milk, rolled around sweetened coconut meat and sometimes flavored with pandan leaves.
A Batak fish dish from North Sumatra, Indonesia, made with raw carp soaked in Kaffir limes and seasoned with andaliman. Its Toba Batak name means “pickled fish.”

An American pie made with butter, sugar, eggs, and flour, using available ingredients when seasonal or costly ones were lacking. It was common before refrigeration and canned fillings, notably during the Great Depression and World War II rationing.

cover.altText: Desperation pie: Shot the pie and ate it. The x100 is great for this sort of thing

list.shortDescription: An Indian dish from Gujarat’s Parsi community, made by cooking chicken or mutton with lentils and vegetables, and served with caramelised rice and fried onions.

cover.altText: Dhansak: Dhansak, a Parsi Dish

list.shortDescription: A Malian barbecue of fire-grilled, seasoned meat cut into pieces and served with grilled or raw onions, mustard, and bread. Street vendors commonly serve it in Mali and Senegal.

cover.altText: Dibi: This is an image with the theme " Farm to Plate " from:

list.shortDescription: A Mexican mixed-meat dish prepared in a discada, a round iron or steel disc pan also used in Southwestern US cooking and nicknamed a cowboy wok.

cover.altText: Discada: mixture of meats and seafood cooked in white wine and covered with sheets ready for cooking vegetables on a platter with coal iron

list.shortDescription: American fries topped with brown gravy and melted shredded cheese, popularized in the 1970s by the Tick Tock Diner in Clifton and commonly served at diners throughout New Jersey.

cover.altText: Disco fries: Disco fries at Hamburger America in September 2025

list.shortDescription: An Indian sweet from Gujarat made with milk, sugar, rice, saffron, and nuts. The milk is slow-boiled until thickened and sweetened, then garnished with chopped dry fruits and nuts and accompanied by pooris.

A Japanese rice gratin of cooked white rice topped with sautéed chicken or shrimp and vegetables, covered with béchamel and cheese, and baked as a casserole. It belongs to yōshoku, Western food adapted to Japanese tastes.

cover.altText: Doria, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: An American peppermint chewing gum made by Wrigley, introduced in the United States in 1914 and advertised as “double strength”; its market share has varied since.

A Danish brand of hard, roughly disc-shaped salmiakki candies with a salty liquorice flavour and no powder filling. Popular in Denmark and Finland, their flavour is strongest on the outside and weakens after a bite.

cover.altText: Dracula Piller, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Hungarian candy of crunchy roasted peanuts coated with sugar, first produced in the 1960s and widely sold by Bonbonetti in blue packaging.

cover.altText: Dunakavics: Dunakavics, the Hungarian roasted peanuts dragée coated with sugar

list.shortDescription: A Nigerian staple made from garri, a dried grated cassava flour, with a slightly sour, sharp taste. It is often eaten with rich soups and stews with beef, stockfish, or mutton.

cover.altText: Eba: Nigerian cassava food called Eba
