cover.altText: Edikang Ikong: Edikang ikong ready to be taken with fufu

list.shortDescription: A traditional Scottish confection of sugar, water, cream of tartar, colourings, and flavourings, shaped into sticks with a soft, crumbly texture.

cover.altText: Edinburgh rock, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Nigerian vegetable soup of the Efik people in Cross River State, made from bitter Editan leaves that are squeezed to remove bitterness before cooking. It is also popular in Akwa Ibom State.
A Nigerian soup known as omoebe, made mainly with scent leaf, uziza leaf, bitter leaf, beef, onion, crayfish powder, pepper, and palm oil. It is popular in Edo State and eaten across Nigeria.

cover.altText: Edo black soup: Schwarzsauer

list.shortDescription: A Yoruba vegetable soup from South West Nigeria, traditionally prepared with locally grown vegetables, meat, fish, and spices. Common additions include spinach, pumpkin leaves, sorrel leaves, peppers, and onions.

cover.altText: Efo riro: This is an image with the theme " Health and Wellness in Africa " from:

list.shortDescription: A popular Yoruba corn porridge from Ibadan, made by cooking dry corn until soft. Served with sauce, beans, and vegetables, it is called ororo robo.

cover.altText: Egbo: Egbo (Food) is a Nigerian Local food. It is popular in the South Western part of the country

list.shortDescription: An Austrian dish of Viennese cuisine, Eiernockerl are egg dumplings. Dumplings are popular in every region of Austria.

cover.altText: Eiernockerl: Eiernockerl mit Speck im Cafe Falk, Wagramer Straße

list.shortDescription: A Chinese dish of glutinous rice steamed with a topping of various ingredients, traditionally eight. Often eaten at celebrations, especially Chinese New Year, its name associates eight with prosperity in Mandarin.

cover.altText: Eight treasure rice: Eight Treasure Rice ba bao fan

list.shortDescription: A Turkish pudding of kadayıf made with ekmek, usually served with kaymak, a clotted cream. Historically a specialty of Afyonkarahisar, it is served at special events there and may be flavored or topped with cherries.

cover.altText: Ekmek kadayıfı: Vişneli ekmek kadayıfı - Ankara

list.shortDescription: A Nigerian and Cameroonian dish of the Bakweri, Bafaw, Oroko, Cross River State, and Akwa Ibom State peoples, made with grated cocoyams wrapped in cocoyam leaves and combined with fish, meat, palm oil, crayfish, periwinkle, and seasoning.

cover.altText: Ekpang Nkwukwo: This is an image of food from

list.shortDescription: A Yoruba dish from Nigeria, Benin, and Togo, Ekuru uses de-hulled black-eyed peas or beans ground plain, mixed until fluffy, wrapped in leaves or tins, and steamed.

cover.altText: Ekuru: This is an image of food from

list.shortDescription: A spicy Bhutanese stew of hot chili peppers and cheese, recognized as the country’s national dish and adapted from Tibetan culinary traditions to suit local tastes.

cover.altText: Ema datshi: Ema datshi (dry red chilli version)

list.shortDescription: A baked or fried turnover made by folding dough around meat, cheese, tomato, corn, or other fillings, common in Spain, Portugal, Latin America, the Philippines, North and West Africa, and South Asia.

cover.altText: Empanadilla: Tapas de empanadillas rellenas de atún y salsa de tomate con huevo cocido

list.shortDescription: A Portuguese convent dessert of egg yolks cooked in sugar syrup and finished under a broiler, believed to have been created at the Convento de Santa Clara in Évora, Alentejo.

cover.altText: Encharcada: doces de ovos

list.shortDescription: A Mexican dish of corn tortillas rolled around a filling and covered in refried bean sauce, typically served with cheese, onions, and crema. Often eaten at breakfast, with regional recipe variations.

cover.altText: Enfrijoladas, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A common Chadian dish of boiled flour, typically served with moulah sauce. It is a staple eaten throughout Chad, often for lunch and dinner, and is also called gou in Zaghawa and tii in Dazaga.

A traditional Catalan salad of shredded salt cod, tomatoes, onions, olive oil, vinegar, and salt, sometimes garnished with olives or hard-boiled eggs. It is popular in warm weather and often served as tapas.

cover.altText: Esqueixada: Esqueixada, catalan cod salad

list.shortDescription: A Vietnamese dessert made with tapioca flour and mung bean filling, wrapped in pandan-leaf boxes and sent by a groom to his bride on their wedding day.

cover.altText: Phu Thê Cake: The traditional Vietnamese wedding cake, Phu The. Phu means man and The means woman. The cake is wrapped in palm leaves in a Hue market

list.shortDescription: Thin round breads from Italy’s Apennines near Modena, made with flour, water, salt and yeast. They can be filled with pork-lard cunza flavored with garlic and rosemary, cold cuts, cheese, or sweet spreads.

cover.altText: Tigella, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: An American dessert of bananas cooked with butter, brown sugar, cinnamon, dark rum, and banana liqueur. The alcohol is ignited tableside, and the bananas and sauce are often served over vanilla ice cream.

cover.altText: bananas Foster: Brennan's Bananas Foster at Brennan's in New Orleans

list.shortDescription: A British dish of sausages with mashed potato, usually served with onion gravy and sometimes fried onions and peas. It is also regarded as pub grub: quick and easy to make in large quantities.

cover.altText: bangers and mash: A plate of sausage, mash, peas and gravy

list.shortDescription: A Korean dish of boiled rice or other grains, including black rice, barley, sorghum, millets, and beans, with vegetables, seafood, or meat added to create variations.

cover.altText: bap: bap (cooked rice)

list.shortDescription: Across India and Pakistan, barfi is a milk-based sweet with a fudge-like texture, especially popular in North India. It is served at celebrations and religious festivals, including Diwali and Holi.

cover.altText: barfi, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A sweet semolina dessert popular across the Middle East, North Africa, the Caucasus, and the Balkans, baked in a sheet pan, soaked in sugar syrup, and cut into diamonds or squares.

cover.altText: basbousa: Unknown description Unknown description Very tasty. Fresh and made at the restaurant

list.shortDescription: An Indian sweet of condensed milk, reduced by half over low heat and sweetened, found mostly in Maharashtra, Gujarat, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Tamil Nadu, and Karnataka. A similar North Indian dish is rabri.

cover.altText: basundi: Basundi in Maharashtrian Style

list.shortDescription: A Malaysian no-bake fridge cake of broken Marie biscuits set with chocolate or egg custard sauce containing condensed milk, Milo, and cocoa. Served at Eid al-Fitr, Christmas, and other festivities.

cover.altText: batik cake: Batik Cake Chocolate Indulgence

list.shortDescription: A standard fish-and-chip-shop item across the United Kingdom: a pork sausage coated in batter, usually the batter used for fish, and served with chips. In Scotland, the meal is called a battered sausage supper.

cover.altText: battered sausage: A cross section of a battered sausage from Trenchers, Whitby

list.shortDescription: A Libyan unleavened bread made by boiling barley or wheat flour in water, beating the dough with a magraf, then baking or steaming it in a pan.

cover.altText: bazeen: bazin

list.shortDescription: A sweet custard pie whose mashed-bean filling combines sugar, eggs, milk, butter, and spices. Common flavorings include vanilla, cinnamon, and nutmeg, with variations adding cloves, ginger, pumpkin pie spice, or lemon extract.

cover.altText: bean pie: This is a picture of bean pies home made by Intisar's Navy Bean Pie recipe from Springfield, MA

list.shortDescription: An American Chinese dish of beef and broccoli, developed by Chinese immigrants in 19th-century America and established in American Chinese restaurants by the 1920s.

cover.altText: beef and broccoli: A plate of American Chinese beef and broccoli

list.shortDescription: A French beef stew braised in red wine and beef stock, flavored with carrots, onions, garlic, and bouquet garni, and garnished with pearl onions and mushrooms.

cover.altText: beef bourguignon: Bœuf bourguignon

list.shortDescription: A Chinese dish of chicken stuffed, wrapped in clay and lotus leaves, then slowly baked over low heat. A single portion may take up to six hours to prepare.

cover.altText: beggar's chicken: Beggar's Chicken by Hangzhou's "Mountain Beyond Mountain" Restaurant

list.shortDescription: A fermented fish condiment from eastern Indonesia, especially around Sulawesi and the Moluccas, made by fermenting fish stomach as shrimp paste is fermented.
A South Korean street snack of silkworm pupae, historically eaten in silk-producing areas and now widely consumed across South Korea.

cover.altText: beondegi: beondegi, street food

list.shortDescription: A Balinese dish of steamed or roasted chicken or duck in rich, highly seasoned bumbu betutu, popular in Bali and Lombok, Indonesia. A spicier version uses raw onion, red chili peppers, and coconut oil.

cover.altText: betutu: A photograph of a Duck dish, known as Bebek Betutu, served with rice and green beans

list.shortDescription: A Gaziantep breakfast soup of lamb neck and cheek with rice, garlic, butter, oil, water, salt, pepper paste, black pepper, and Aleppo pepper flakes.

cover.altText: beyran: Beyran, a soup from Gaziantep, Turkey

list.shortDescription: A Chinese noodle from Shaanxi cuisine, also called yóupō chěmiàn, noted for its great thickness and length and counted among the Eight Curiosities of Shaanxi.

cover.altText: biangbiang noodles: Biang Biang Mian closeup

list.shortDescription: A light Turkish dessert associated with southern Turkey and the Mediterranean, especially Adana and Mersin, where it is eaten in summer. Its name comes from the sound of starch being squeezed between the fingers.

cover.altText: bici bici: Adana iline özgü bir tür tatlı olan Bici bici

list.shortDescription: A Polish hunter’s stew of chopped assorted meats cooked with sauerkraut, shredded fresh cabbage, and spices. Served hot, it may be enriched with vegetables or wine.

cover.altText: bigos: Bigos, Restaurant am Rathaus: Karczma Lwowska, Wroclaw / Breslau

list.shortDescription: A Korean milk-based shaved ice dessert. The common patbingsu variety is topped with sweet red beans, while other versions may include chopped fruit, condensed milk, fruit syrup, and tteok.

cover.altText: bingsu: patbingsu

list.shortDescription: A Gorontalese sweet corn soup from Sulawesi, Indonesia, served hot with shredded coconut, basil leaves, skipjack tuna, and shrimp.

cover.altText: binte biluhuta, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A non-alcoholic drink of Jakarta’s Betawi people, made with ginger, pandan leaves, boiled sappan wood, and lemongrass, and known as a “beer” despite containing no alcohol.

cover.altText: bir pletok: Bir pletok, minuman tradisional khas masyarakat Betawi di Jakarta

list.shortDescription: A popular Southern American breakfast of soft dough biscuits covered in white sausage gravy made from pork drippings, flour, milk, and bits of meat, often seasoned with black pepper.

cover.altText: biscuits and gravy, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: Sicilian biscuits prepared for the feast of San Martino di Tours on November 11. The hard version, called tricotto, is anise-flavored, baked three times, and traditionally soaked in wine.

cover.altText: biscuits of Saint Martin: Biscotto di San Martino tipo duro confezionato

list.shortDescription: A sweet Nordic fruit soup made from bilberries, with starch giving it a thick consistency. It can be served cold or hot, as a soup with porridge or as a drink.

cover.altText: blåbärssoppa: A cup of bilberry ( Vaccinium myrtillus ) soup with roasted coconut flakes

list.shortDescription: A South African dish of spiced minced meat baked with an egg-based topping, adopted by the Cape Malay community and often served with sambal. It is not a national dish.

cover.altText: bobotie: Bobotie, Südafrikanisches Gericht

list.shortDescription: A Colombian candy made from guava pulp and panela, known as guava jelly or paste and eaten throughout Colombia, Costa Rica, Ecuador, Panama, and Venezuela. Similar versions use banana or coconut.

cover.altText: bocadillo: Colombian bocadillo

list.shortDescription: An Italian pastry typical of Abruzzo, Apulia, and Calabria, often eaten at Christmas. Its filling varies by region; in Abruzzo it may include cocoa powder, cinnamon, and toasted almonds.

cover.altText: bocconotto: Bocconotto bought at Clementi, just outside Castel Frentano, CH, Italy

list.shortDescription: A Cape Malay milk pudding of vermicelli, sago, and sugar, flavoured with cardamom, stick cinnamon, and rose water. It is served on the 15th night of Ramadan to celebrate the middle of the fast.

cover.altText: boeber: This is an image of food from

list.shortDescription: A Botswana porridge made with lerotse, an orange-fleshed citron melon resembling a watermelon, whose neutral raw flavor becomes distinctive when cooked.

cover.altText: bogobe jwa lerotse: This is an image of "African people at work" from

list.shortDescription: An Italian mixed boil of tougher beef and veal cuts, cotechino, and a whole hen or capon, simmered in aromatic vegetable stock.

cover.altText: bollito misto: Gran bollito misto piemontese, piatto tipico a base di varie carni bollite accompagnate da verdure e ortaggi bolliti, salse e mostarda

list.shortDescription: A Portuguese rice muffin common in Portugal, Lusophone countries and regions, and places with significant Portuguese immigrant populations, including Canada, Australia, Luxembourg, the United States, and France.

cover.altText: bolo de arroz: Bolo de Arroz (Lisbon)

list.shortDescription: A Belgian brioche-style pastry made with flour, milk, butter, cassonade, and raisins, shaped into a spiral and especially associated with Brussels.

cover.altText: bolus, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A French ice cream dessert frozen in a spherical mould to resemble a cannonball, giving rise to the name ice cream bomb. It appeared on restaurant menus by 1882, and Escoffier lists more than sixty recipes for it.

cover.altText: bombe glacée, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Mongolian meat dish of goat, mutton, or Tarbagan marmot cooked with heated stones inserted into the deboned carcass and often accompanied by vegetables. It is prepared for special occasions.

cover.altText: boodog: Mongolian hunter prepares a boodog using a marmot

list.shortDescription: A Korean pork dish of belly boiled in spices and thinly sliced, served with spicy radish salad, raw garlic, ssamjang, saeu-jeot, kimchi, and lettuce, perilla, and napa cabbage leaves for wrapping.

cover.altText: bossam, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Javanese dish made from grated coconut flesh with the coconut milk squeezed out, often mixed with vegetables or fish, wrapped in banana leaf, and steamed. It has a soft, mozzarella-like texture and is usually white.

cover.altText: botok: Bubur Lolos (left) and Botok Roti (right), traditional snacks from Cirebon

list.shortDescription: A Provençal fish soup from Marseille, first made by fishermen with bony rockfish, now prepared with seafood and vegetables in a herb-spiced broth and served with bread and rouille.

cover.altText: bouillabaisse, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: An Algerian pastry of thin “dyoul” sheets filled with mashed potatoes, chopped onions, cumin and paprika. Folded into triangles, rectangles or spirals, it is baked or deep-fried until golden and crispy.

cover.altText: bourek: Algerian bourek

list.shortDescription: Bourekas are baked turnovers in Israeli and Sephardic Jewish cuisine, made in varied shapes with numerous fillings and enclosed in puff pastry, filo dough, or brik pastry.

cover.altText: bourekas: A Photograph of three small Cheese Bourekases and Two "Turkish" Potato-filled Bourekases from Israel

list.shortDescription: A Thessaloniki meze of feta, tomatoes, peppers, oregano, olive oil, and crushed red pepper, layered in an earthenware dish and baked, sometimes with kasseri, onions, and garlic.

cover.altText: bouyiourdi: Thessalonikian bouyiourdi made in a clay fireproof pan. The recipe consists of feta cheese, yellow cheese, tomatoes, bell pepper, chili pepper, olive oil, oregano, and ground pepper

list.shortDescription: A traditional meat stew, sometimes described as soup, popular in Armenia, Azerbaijan, and Iran. Its meatball version resembles a gray head after cooking.

cover.altText: bozbash: Tikə bozbaş

list.shortDescription: An Indonesian fermented food or drink with a solid snack cake from Madiun and Wonogiri and a liquid rice wine from Bali and Nusa Tenggara, especially Bali. It first appeared in Java around 1000.

cover.altText: brem: Brem, traditional fermented food of Indonesia

list.shortDescription: An English potato dish of cooked potatoes and cabbage mixed together and fried. Its history reaches back at least to the 18th century; it once included cooked beef, but the vegetables became its principal ingredients by the mid-20th.

cover.altText: bubble and squeak, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Southeast Asian sweet porridge of boiled mung beans with coconut milk and palm or cane sugar, also called burjo.

cover.altText: bubur kacang hijau: Mung bean porridge

list.shortDescription: Historically, burrito was a regional Mexican name for a taco, used in Guanajuato, Guerrero, Michoacán, San Luis Potosí, Sonora, and Sinaloa. Mexico City’s influence made “taco” the default; the name was forgotten.

cover.altText: burrito, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Vietnamese street-food bun adapted from Cantonese tai pao, with seasoned ground pork and quail egg as a common filling. It may contain Chinese sausage and is typically eaten at breakfast or as a snack.

cover.altText: bánh bao, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A steamed Vietnamese cake from Huế, Central Vietnam, whose name refers to a small, round-leaved aquatic plant resembling duckweed or water lily; the cake imitates that plant’s shape.

cover.altText: bánh bèo: Glutinous rice, meat, ground peanuts, fish sauce

list.shortDescription: A Vietnamese cake of glutinous rice, mung beans, and pork, wrapped in a square green package. At Tết, it is placed on family altars to honor ancestors; its square form symbolizes the earth.

cover.altText: bánh chưng, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A northern Vietnamese rice cake made from sticky rice, sugar, gac or gardenia, sesame, carrots, mandarin orange peel, and lard. Its roasted, ground mixture is placed in a square box and traditionally served with tea.

cover.altText: bánh cáy: Bánh cáy, làng Nguyễn, Thái Bình

list.shortDescription: A Vietnamese street food associated with Lâm Đồng, made with sweet potato or cassava. Sweet-potato pancakes are deep-fried and sugared. They take their name from rế, Vietnamese for bamboo baskets, which they resemble.

cover.altText: bánh rế, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Vietnamese savoury, sometimes sweetened cake of glutinous rice, rolled with mung bean and pork in banana leaf into a thick cylinder, then boiled, unwrapped, and sliced into wheel-shaped servings.

cover.altText: bánh tét, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Vietnamese pastry specialty of Hải Dương province, bánh đậu xanh is made from mung beans, sugar, and lard or vegetable oil.

cover.altText: bánh đậu xanh: Vietnamese green bean cake

list.shortDescription: A Middle Eastern filo dough dessert called “nightingale’s nest” for its hollow, circular shape. After baking, warm syrup is sprinkled on it, the center filled with walnuts or pistachios, and a walnut half set on top.

cover.altText: bülbülyuvası: Bülbülyuvası amb nous en comptes dels pistachios convencionals

list.shortDescription: A Chinese corn soup similar to cream of corn soup, with egg white and crab meat or imitation crab meat added.

cover.altText: corn crab soup, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: An American hot dog made by placing a sausage on a stick, coating it with thick cornmeal batter, and deep-frying it.
Indonesian corn fritters are fried cakes made from dough or batter containing corn kernels, known as perkedel jagung or bakwan jagung.

cover.altText: corn fritter: Barranquilla maize buñuelos (sweet corn fritters)

list.shortDescription: An English salad of boneless chicken seasoned with parsley, thyme, bay, cumin, turmeric, ginger and peppercorns, mixed with cream or mayonnaise and dried apricots, served cold with rice, peas and pimentos.

cover.altText: coronation chicken: Coronation chicken

list.shortDescription: An Indonesian soup from Makassar, South Sulawesi, with beef and innards such as intestine, liver, lungs, heart, tripe, or cow brain in a broth seasoned with ground peanuts and spices.

cover.altText: coto makassar, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: An American fishcake of crab meat mixed with bread crumbs, mayonnaise, mustard, eggs, and seasonings, then sautéed, baked, grilled, deep-fried, or broiled. It is traditionally associated with Maryland’s Chesapeake Bay.

cover.altText: crab cake: A Delicious Crabcake at the Middleton Tavern

list.shortDescription: A Scottish dessert made to celebrate the August raspberry harvest, with cream, seasonal raspberries, Scottish oats, and whisky. Its roots lie in crowdie, a breakfast of cheese, toasted oatmeal, cream, and local honey.

cover.altText: cranachan: The best Scottish dessert

list.shortDescription: A Japanese meat dish of chicken or pork with onion, carrot, potato, cabbage, and mixed vegetables, simmered in thick white roux. Milk may replace water for extra creaminess.

cover.altText: cream stew, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A French deep-fried roll of a thick binder combined with a filling, then breaded and served worldwide as a side dish, snack, or fast food.

cover.altText: crocchè, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: Italian crostini are small slices of grilled or toasted bread topped with cheeses, meats, vegetables, condiments, or simply brushed with olive oil and herbs.

cover.altText: crostini: Spinach and cheese crostini

list.shortDescription: French appetizers of raw vegetables, cut or left whole and typically served with vinaigrette or a sauce for dipping. Celery, carrot, cucumber, bell pepper, and fennel are examples; bagna càuda and pinzimonio are sauces.

cover.altText: crudités: Veggie platter

list.shortDescription: A dish made from unleavened batter or dough cooked on a frying pan or griddle, with sweet or savoury versions filled with cheese, fruit, vegetables, meats, or spreads.

cover.altText: crêpe: Crepe

list.shortDescription: A traditional British crustless tea sandwich made with thin cucumber slices between two thin slices of lightly buttered white bread.

cover.altText: cucumber sandwich: Ready for a tea party

list.shortDescription: A thick Scottish fish soup of smoked haddock, potatoes, and onions. Authentic versions use finnan haddie, though other undyed smoked haddock, ocean perch, or salmon may also be used.

cover.altText: cullen skink: A bowl of cullen skink, served with bread

list.shortDescription: An outer pastry shell surrounds custard in this baked tart, also known as flan pâtissier or flan parisien.

cover.altText: custard tart, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: An Indonesian jajan pasar, especially in Java: a green rice-flour pancake colored with pandan or suji leaves, folded and filled with grated coconut and palm sugar.

cover.altText: dadar gulung: Kue dadar gulung

list.shortDescription: A Belgian sandwich of baguette filled with ham, cheese, and raw vegetables, called a dagobert in Wallonia, a club in Brussels, or Smos in Flanders.

A Nigerien cereal-and-moringa dish native to the Zarma and Songhai of southwestern Niger, eaten at any time but mainly during outdoor gatherings and weddings. It is also common among the Dendi of northern Benin.

cover.altText: dambu, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A northern Nigerian dish of boiled dumplings made from cowpea flour, usually garnished with sauce, egg, vegetables, or chili pepper. The dumplings have little flavor on their own.

cover.altText: danwake: A Hausa Food called Dan wake, made from either grind beans or grind cassava

list.shortDescription: Thinly sliced dried meat in Minangkabau cuisine, preserved with sugar and spices and dried by frying. It is sweet and spicy, similar to jerky, and remains stable for several weeks at room temperature.

cover.altText: dendeng: Dendeng batokok

list.shortDescription: A hot appetizer of cheese- or nut-stuffed dried fruit wrapped in bacon, prosciutto, or pancetta, then fried or baked. Dates are traditional; prunes are also used, usually steeped in brandy or liqueur.

cover.altText: devils on horseback: Devils on Horseback

list.shortDescription: A Gujarati savoury sponge cake made from fermented rice-and-chickpea batter and steamed to a cake-like consistency. Variants replace the chickpea with pigeon peas or urad beans.

cover.altText: dhokla, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A fish dish of salmon wrapped in aluminum foil and cooked through a full dishwasher cycle, though inconsistent dishwasher temperatures pose a risk of food poisoning.

cover.altText: dishwasher salmon, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: Japan’s dobin mushi is a traditional broth of shrimp, chicken, soy sauce, lime, and matsutake mushroom, steamed and served in a dobin tea pot.

cover.altText: dobin mushi: A Japanese broth served in a small teapot

list.shortDescription: Dolma names a family of stuffed dishes largely associated with Ottoman cuisine. Vegetables and leaves are hollowed or wrapped, then filled with rice, minced meat, herbs, and spices.

cover.altText: dolmadakiа: Gatim tradicional Kosovarëi njohur si speca dollma nga turqishtja

list.shortDescription: Turkish ice cream made with cream, salep, mastic, and sugar. Outside the Middle East, dondurma often means mastic ice cream, associated with Kahramanmaraş and called maraş dondurma.

cover.altText: dondurma: Maraş "dondurma" with kabak (pumpkin) sauce

list.shortDescription: A Nigerian soup of okra, ogbono, or ewedu leaves. Its thick broth draws out of the bowl when eaten by spoon or used to dip fufu, inspiring the Pidgin English name. It accompanies eba (garri) and pounded yam.

cover.altText: draw soup: This is an image with the theme " Health and Wellness in Africa " from:

list.shortDescription: A layered salad of diced spekesild covered with grated boiled eggs, vegetables, chopped onions, and mayonnaise. Known as shuba or “furry herring,” some versions also include fresh grated apple.

cover.altText: dressed herring, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Thai stir-fried noodle dish similar to phat si-io but spicier. Its name means “drunkard” because it is popular among the inebriated, although alcohol is not used.

cover.altText: drunken noodles, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Chinese dish of freshwater shrimp immersed in liquor to make them easier to consume. Regional versions serve the shrimp raw, cook them in boiling water, or marinate cooked shrimp in rice wine.

cover.altText: drunken shrimp, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A traditional South American jellied dessert eaten across the Southern Cone, served plain, with cheese, or with chocolate. Local names include dulce de boniatos and Brazil’s marrom glacê or doce de batata doce.

cover.altText: dulce de batata: Dulce de batata with chocolate

list.shortDescription: A Canadian square, yeast-raised doughnut containing raisins and covered in sugary glaze. It gained popularity through Tim Hortons, whose menu has included it as one of two original baked goods since 1964.

cover.altText: dutchie, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A South Korean pork soup especially associated with Busan, made with soy sauce, miso, rice wine, sesame oil, and bone broth. Rice, kimchi, garlic, green peppers, and other sides can be added.

cover.altText: dwaeji-gukbap: dwaeji-gukbap (pork and rice soup) with kkakdugi (diced radish kimchi)

list.shortDescription: A Turkish soup made with lamb or beef broth, now eaten daily mainly in winter. It first opened village wedding feasts, which tradition held could last forty days and forty nights.

cover.altText: düğün çorbası, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: Indonesian curry-like beef soup from Cirebon, West Java, made with beef, intestine, tripe, and lungs cooked in coconut milk with garlic, chilies, chives, and sambal in a firewood-fired gentong stove.

cover.altText: empal gentong: Cirebon's ethnic food

list.shortDescription: A Mexican dish of corn tortillas rolled around meat, cheese, beans, potatoes, vegetables, or combinations of fillings, then covered with chili-, tomato-, mole-, or cheese-based sauce.

cover.altText: enchilada: Enchilada, rice, and beans

list.shortDescription: An Indonesian iced fruit dessert of diced honeydew, cantaloupe, pineapple, papaya, squash, jackfruit, and kolang kaling mixed with ice and sweetened with sugar or syrup.

cover.altText: es buah, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: An Indonesian coconut-milk shaved-ice drink and dessert, a specialty of Bandung, West Java, with pink syrup, condensed milk, avocado, cassava tapai, ketan hitam tapai, jackfruit, diced bread, and pacar cina merah delima.

cover.altText: es doger, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Sundanese cold drink from Indonesia made with shaved ice, coconut milk, sugar syrup, and jellied mung bean starch called hunkwe. Avocado and shredded coconut may also be added.

cover.altText: es goyobod, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: Portuguese skewer dishes often use beef or pork with bell pepper, onion and chouriço, served with rice, potatoes or salad. In Madeira, beef cubes seasoned with salt, garlic and bay leaf grill over hot coals.

cover.altText: espetada: Hotel "Quinta Alegre" in Estreito da Calheta, Madeira. Es handelt sich um Rindfleisch auf Spießen aus grünem Lorbeerholz

list.shortDescription: A traditional Malay porridge from Sambas, West Kalimantan, and Sarawak, Malaysia, served during Ramadan when Muslims break their fast at iftar.

cover.altText: spicy porridge: Spicy porridge; Sambas special cullinary

list.shortDescription: A buttery, flaky viennoiserie bread roll filled with pastry cream, sometimes flavored with rosemary. Its layered yeast-leavened dough is folded with butter to create a flaky texture.

cover.altText: torpedo dessert: Tube with a crisp pastry filled with custard cream

list.shortDescription: A Cajun and Creole dish of shellfish served over rice, prepared through the smothering method common in South Louisiana.

cover.altText: étouffée: Crawfish etouffee

list.shortDescription: A traditional pastry from western Guangdong, China, made of glutinous rice cakes on banana leaves and shared with relatives and friends during festivals, weddings, birthdays, and housewarming parties.

cover.altText: 籺(hé): traditional Maoming snack

list.shortDescription: A dense, moist Christmas cake from Italy’s Romagna and San Marino, made with flour, cornmeal, leavening, olive oil or shortening, sugar or honey, breadcrumbs, dried fruit, apples, and citrus rind.

cover.altText: Bustrengo: Bustrengo prepared with polenta, apple, fig and toffee. 'Amore Dogs', Edinburgh

list.shortDescription: A sweet, cold Danish dairy drink made with buttermilk and varying additions including eggs, sugar, yoghurt, vanilla, and sometimes lemon, eaten chilled as a dessert or snack.

cover.altText: Buttermilk koldskål: Koldskål served with strawberries and kammerjunker

list.shortDescription: A Cape Verdean national dish of slowly cooked hominy, beans, fish or meat, often with morcela. Each island has its own variation, from richer cachupa rica to simpler cachupa pobre.

cover.altText: Cachupa: Cachupa

list.shortDescription: A South African Cadbury chocolate bar with a shortcake biscuit surrounded by smooth, creamy caramel and coated in dairy milk chocolate.
A traditional soup from Galicia, known simply as caldo or caldo gallego, this dish is a regional variation of neighboring Portugal’s caldo verde.

cover.altText: Caldo galego: Caldo gallego

list.shortDescription: An American sushi of imitation crab, avocado, and cucumber, sometimes using crab salad in place of the crab stick. It is often served as uramaki, with outside rice sprinkled with toasted sesame seeds or roe.

cover.altText: California roll: California Sushi

list.shortDescription: A crown-shaped Corsican Easter cake made from yeast dough, with boiled eggs resembling bells inside its bell-tower form. The eggs signify renewed fertility after winter and recall bells released at Easter.
An Italian goat-and-bean stew from Imperia’s hinterland, made with goat meat, preferably shoulder, slowly cooked with onions, carrots, celery, white wine, and white beans.
An Italian salad of sliced fresh mozzarella, tomatoes, and basil, seasoned with salt and olive oil or balsamic vinegar. Its name references Capri, where it is believed to have originated.

cover.altText: Caprese salad: Insalata caprese , made from mozzarella, tomatoes, olive oil and basil. Own work

list.shortDescription: A Costa Rican meal of rice, black beans, plantains, salad, and a tortilla, with an optional protein such as chicken, beef, pork, or fish.

cover.altText: Casado: A Costa Rican lunch, called casado . Comes with rice, fried plantain, onioned meat (chicken or beef), an egg, beans and a cabbage salad sprinkled with lemon juice and salt

list.shortDescription: A Sicilian cake of sponge cake moistened with fruit juice or liqueur, layered with ricotta and candied fruit, and covered with marzipan, pink and green icing, and decorative designs.

cover.altText: Cassata siciliana PAT, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Sicilian pastry from Catania made for Saint Agatha’s February 3–5 festival. Round sponge cakes soaked in rosolio are filled with sheep’s-milk ricotta, chocolate drops, and candied citrus, then coated in white icing and topped with a candied cherry.

cover.altText: Cassatella di Sant'Agata: La spécialité de Catane : les seins d'Agathe

list.shortDescription: A festive Burmese salad of Siamese cassia flower buds, boiled potatoes, sliced onions, peanuts, sesame seeds, garlic, salt, oil, and lemon juice, served on the full-moon day of Tazaungmon, sometimes as an offering.

A Spanish sweetmeat typical of Vilafranca del Penedès and nearby towns: toasted marcona almonds covered with caramel, then white chocolate or an almond, hazelnut and milk mixture, and powdered black chocolate.

cover.altText: Catànies: Catànies

list.shortDescription: A lamb kebab from Erzurum Province, Turkey, with marinated meat stacked horizontally on a rotating spit over a wood fire.

cover.altText: Cağ kebabı: Cağ Kebabı of Erzurum in Turkey - General view of the spit

list.shortDescription: A Puebla sandwich served on a sesame-seeded roll, usually filled with sliced avocado, meat, Oaxaca cheese, pápalo, chipotle adobado, or jalapeño.

cover.altText: Cemita: Cemita bread at the Cemita market in Puebla, Mexico

list.shortDescription: An Indonesian dessert of green, worm-like jelly strands made with rice flour or mung bean starch, flavored with pandan and served over shaved ice with coconut milk and palm sugar syrup.

cover.altText: Cendol: Cendol di Kampung Paya Jaras Tengah, Daerah Petaling, Selangor, Malaysia

list.shortDescription: A traditional snack also called cendil or cetil, made from tapioca dough and sugar, usually colored and shaped into small balls or cubes, then coated and eaten with grated coconut.

cover.altText: Cenil: Penganan tradisional Jawa

list.shortDescription: Certs is a breath-mint brand known for the slogan “two mints in one.” Its original mints were disc-shaped without holes and sold in roll packaging similar to Life Savers and Polo.

Chajá, a Uruguayan dessert, dates to April 27, 1927, when Orlando Castellano launched it at Confitería Las Familias in Paysandú. It is a semi-industrial export to Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, and the United States.

cover.altText: Chajá: Massini, chajá y otros postres

list.shortDescription: A thick, warm Mexican chocolate drink made with masa, corn flour, or masa harina, piloncillo, milk or water, and chocolate, then whisked with a molinillo; cinnamon, aniseed, vanilla, nuts, orange zest, or egg may be added.

cover.altText: Champurrado, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A traditional Georgian lamb stew with tomatoes, aubergines, potatoes, greens, and garlic, layered in individual clay pots, slow-cooked in the oven for 4.5–5 hours, and served with bread and cheese.

cover.altText: Chanakhi: Chanakhi, Chanaki, Chenaki

list.shortDescription: A Chinese dish famous in Beijing, made by simmering pork liver and pork intestine with starch, garlic, vinegar, and soy sauce, and traditionally served with baozi.

cover.altText: Chaogan: 18 for this large serving, and 14 for smaller serving

list.shortDescription: A South Korean instant noodle brand by Nongshim, first released on 19 March 1984. It was the country’s first instant noodle resembling Chinese jajangmyeon, and its name combines jajangmyeon with spaghetti.

cover.altText: Chapagetti: Nongshim Instant chajang noodles <Chapagetti>

list.shortDescription: An American lollipop from the Charms Candy Company, founded in 1912 in Bloomfield, New Jersey. Tootsie Roll acquired the company in 1988 and added Blow Pops to its product line.
A French dish of cabbage, chicory, or carrot wrapped in a decorative layer of salad or vegetable leaves and cooked in a dome mould. Variations have existed since at least the eighteenth century.

cover.altText: Chartreuse: Chartreuse de pintadeau de la Drôme

list.shortDescription: Chewz is a Mentos-like brand-name confectionery made by Lance, Inc., with a hard shell and soft, chewy interior. Mentos fans call it “Anti-Mentos.”
A traditional Indian bread from Jharkhand made with rice flour and chana dal, soaked overnight, ground into batter, and roasted on a greased tawa. Served with chutney, vegetables, and meat.

cover.altText: Chhilka Roti: Chilka Roti, the traditional dish of Jharkhand. It is prepared using rice flour and dal

list.shortDescription: A staple in Cameroon and across Central Africa, chikwangue is made by fermenting cassava in water for up to fourteen days, then wrapping the paste in marantaceae leaves for steaming.

cover.altText: Chikwangue, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Mexican stuffed pepper, usually a poblano, filled with melted cheese or pork picadillo with raisins and nuts. It can be coated in egg white or corn masa and fried, or left unbattered; it is often served in tomato sauce.

cover.altText: Chile relleno: A photograph of Chile Rellenos, stuffed Chile peppers

list.shortDescription: Chinmi are Japanese delicacies: local cuisines that have fallen from popularity or are peculiar to certain regions, many involving pickled seafood.

cover.altText: Chinmi: Karasumi, a fishery product made by salting mullet roe and drying it in sunlight

list.shortDescription: A South Indian lemon rice seasoned with mustard seeds, fried lentils, peanuts, curry leaves, chillies, lemon juice, and turmeric, with optional unripe mango and sometimes garlic and onions. It is a daily dish in Karnataka.

cover.altText: Chitranna: Chitranna is prepared with rice and lemon with nice blend of seeds and vegitables

list.shortDescription: A French chocolate dessert made with dark chocolate, butter, sugar, cocoa powder, eggs, and cream, possibly linked to the Marquise de Sévigné.

cover.altText: Chocolate marquise: Chocolate marquise with crème anglaise and roasted pistachios

list.shortDescription: A pizza made with chocolate as its primary ingredient and prepared in varied styles and techniques. It may be made as either a dessert or a savory dish.

cover.altText: Chocolate pizza: Pizza made using chocolate in Brazil

list.shortDescription: A Ukrainian chocolate candy created as an April Fool’s joke in the late 1990s, with caramel filling and a small amount of rendered fat for salty flavor.

cover.altText: Chocolate salo: Сало в шоколаді

list.shortDescription: A traditional Christmas Eve dish in Central Europe, with carp kept in a bathtub to remove muddy flavours before being fried or served as gefilte fish.

cover.altText: Christmas carp: Christmas carp with potato salad, tradicional Czech christmas

list.shortDescription: An Andean soup or stew from the mountains of South America, made in large portions for marketplaces and events and sometimes served with wine as a warming food in the cold climate.

An Italian ring-shaped cake with regional variations. A basic version combines flour, baking powder, salt, eggs, milk, sugar, oil, and vanilla, with honey sometimes added; the sugar and eggs are whisked before baking in a ring-shaped pan.
An Indonesian ball-shaped dumpling made from aci, a Sundanese snack, pierced with lidi skewers made from the midribs of coconut palm fronds.

cover.altText: Cilok: Hakaneun tina tipung

list.shortDescription: Indonesian cakes made by the Karo of North Sumatra from rice flour, coconut, and palm sugar, with varieties fried like pancakes, wrapped in singkut leaves, or cooked inside bamboo.
Italian PGI specialty chocolate from Modica, Sicily, made by manual grinding and a traditional cold, unconched process that gives it a grainy texture and aromatic flavor.

cover.altText: Cioccolato di Modica PGI, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: An American entrée of meat cubes, usually pork, threaded on wooden skewers and fried or baked, sometimes breaded. Despite its name, it rarely contains chicken.

cover.altText: City chicken: An example of City Chicken, found in Pittsburgh, PA

list.shortDescription: A New England savory meat pie made with clams, especially quahogs, likely predating English settlement in Southern New England as a feature of Indigenous peoples’ diets.

cover.altText: Clam pie: Curry clam pie

list.shortDescription: A Mott’s commercial drink of reconstituted tomato juice concentrate and sugar, flavored with spices, dried clam broth, and MSG. It is often mixed with alcohol to make a Caesar.

A traditional coconut confectionery found in many parts of Latin America and Europe, popular in Mexico, Argentina, Bolivia, Brazil, Colombia, Chile, Cuba, Spain, Panama, Venezuela, Ecuador, and the Dominican Republic.

cover.altText: Cocada: Cocadas, sobremesa típica de Ferrol, Galiza

list.shortDescription: A Canarian rabbit dish marinated in white wine, olive oil, and often vinegar with garlic, bay leaf, bell peppers, and thyme, then sautéed and cooked in the marinade; liver is often included.

cover.altText: Conejo en salmorejo: Conejo en salmorejo y Lasaña (králík a lasaně), restaurace Estrellas, Guía de Isora, provincie Santa Cruz de Tenerife 02

list.shortDescription: A French clear soup made from richly flavoured stock or broth, clarified with egg whites or gelatin filtration. It is commonly based on beef or veal, with chicken, fish, and game variants, and may be served alone or used in soups, sauces, and stews.

cover.altText: Consommé: self-made consommé de volaille (double consomme soup with chicken)

list.shortDescription: A sourdough bread from Ferrara, Italy, made around the 13th century with flour, lard, malt, and olive oil, and shaped in twists. It received EU protected geographical indication status in 2001.

cover.altText: Coppia Ferrarese PGI: Coppia Ferrarese è il nome di un pane prodotto nella provincia di Ferrara - Italia

list.shortDescription: A Chinese stir-fry of thinly sliced Erkuai fried with pork, egg, soy sauce, and vegetables. It is commonly paired with soup but can also be eaten alone.

cover.altText: Da jiu-jia: ​腾冲大救驾

list.shortDescription: A Yoruba street food of Yorubaland across Togo, Nigeria, and Benin, made from soft-mashed beans stewed with bell peppers, onion, ginger, dried chilies, dried crayfish powder, and palm oil. Commonly eaten with bread.

cover.altText: Ewa Agoyin: This is an image with the theme " Health and Wellness in Africa " from:

list.shortDescription: Extra, a Wrigley brand of sugarfree chewing gum, launched in the United States in 1984 and reached several world markets with variations. It was the first sugarfree gum to use aspartame instead of saccharin.

cover.altText: Extra: Packaging of Wrigley's Extra chewing gum

list.shortDescription: A rich bean stew from the Principality of Asturias, also called fabada, available throughout Spain and in Spanish restaurants worldwide. Canned versions are sold in most supermarkets countrywide.

cover.altText: Fabada asturiana: Fabada en cazuela de barro

list.shortDescription: Farl are quadrant-shaped flatbreads and cakes, traditionally made by dividing a round into four. In Ulster, the name generally means soda bread and, less often, potato bread, both ingredients in an Ulster fry.

cover.altText: Farl: A Soda bread farl. This farl would have been connected to the others along the top and right hand straight edges

list.shortDescription: Fatias de Tomar (“Slices of Tomar”) is a Portuguese dessert from Tomar. Nuns in the Convent of Christ originally made it.

cover.altText: Fatias de Tomar: Fatias de Tomar

list.shortDescription: Fatoot samneh is a Yemeni dish of saluf, malawach, or pita fried in clarified butter and combined with beaten egg. Served at breakfast or dinner, it was brought to Israel by Yemenite Jews.

cover.altText: Fatoot samneh: A photo of the Yemenite-Jewish Israeli dish Fatoot Samneh

list.shortDescription: An Italian pasta of fettuccine combined with butter and Parmesan, emulsified into a rich sauce that coats the noodles. It arose in Rome in the early 20th century.

cover.altText: Fettuccine Alfredo: Fettuccine Alfredo da "Il vero Alfredo" a Roma

list.shortDescription: An English savoury pie layered with apple, cured pork, onion, and sometimes potato beneath a crimped shortcrust pastry top. It is especially popular in Shropshire, where sugar and sweet spices are added.

cover.altText: Fidget pie, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: Filipino spaghetti adapts Italian spaghetti with a sweet Bolognese sauce: tomato sauce sweetened with brown sugar, banana ketchup, or condensed milk. It is topped with hot dogs or longganisa, giniling, and grated cheese.

cover.altText: Filipino spaghetti: Red hot dogs, ground beef, Kraft "Cheese" (grated), a single bottle of Jufran Banana Ketchup, a can of Del Monte Traditional Spaghetti Sauce, onions, garlic, brown sugar, salt, pepper

list.shortDescription: A British chocolate bar made by Cadbury, formed from thinly folded milk chocolate and oils and known for its crumbly texture.
Mexican flautas are larger rolled tacos filled with beef, cheese, or chicken, then shallow- or deep-fried. They use flour or corn tortillas and are often topped with sour cream or guacamole.

cover.altText: Flauta: Burros & Fries Clairemont Mesa

list.shortDescription: A pink, scented candy shaped like an inflated strawberry and coated in fine sugar, invented by Haribo in 1969 and made with sugar, glucose syrup, gelatin, citric acid, flavoring, and colorings.

cover.altText: Fraise Tagada: The Fraise Tagada (Tagada Strawberry) is a candy invented in 1969 by the Haribo Society

list.shortDescription: A thin parboiled sausage packed in sheep’s intestine casing and flavoured by low-temperature smoking. Traditionally served with bread, mustard, horseradish, or potato salad.

cover.altText: Frankfurter Würstchen: Ein Paar Frankfurter auf Kartoffelsalat

list.shortDescription: An American hot sandwich of thinly sliced roast beef on a French roll or baguette, served with a cup of beef broth for dipping.

cover.altText: French dip sandwich: Roast beef dip, french fries, au jus, ketchup, beer and fire in background

list.shortDescription: An American dip of sour cream flavored with minced onion and dehydrated French onion soup mix, served with potato chips, snack crackers, or crudités. Despite its name, it is not French cuisine.

cover.altText: French onion dip, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A French fast-food dish from Lyon, also called a matelas, with a grilled flour tortilla folded around French fries, cheese, meat, and other deli ingredients.

cover.altText: French tacos: French "tacos" from O'Tacos

list.shortDescription: Vendors in Tunisia sell a savory, yeast-raised bread that is fried and often stuffed with tuna, hard-boiled egg, olives, harissa, preserved lemons, capers, and mashed potato, with turmeric as a condiment.

cover.altText: Fricasse: Le fricassé ou frit cassé est un beignet salé issu de la tradition culinaire tunisienne

list.shortDescription: An Acadian stew of chicken, potatoes, onions, carrots, and summer savoury, sometimes with dumplings. The call to eat in Acadian French is “Au fricot!”

cover.altText: Fricot: Fricot

list.shortDescription: Fried potato-and-leek pancakes common in Sephardic Jewish cuisine, also known as keftes de prasa or albondigas de prasa.

cover.altText: Fritas de prasa: Fritas or Fritikas or Keftikas de Prasa is a traditional Sepharadi food, mainly from the Balkans and Turkey

list.shortDescription: A Sicilian marzipan sweet shaped like fruits and vegetables and colored with vegetable dyes, from Palermo and Trapani. The tradition is said to have begun at La Martorana nunnery, where marzipan fruit decorated bare trees.

cover.altText: Frutti di Martorana PAT: Frutta di Martorana

list.shortDescription: An Argentine pizza from Buenos Aires with a thick crust, topped with onions and sometimes olives. Fugazza con queso adds mozzarella.

cover.altText: Fugazza: Pizza

list.shortDescription: A savory breakfast from Tianjin, China, Guoba cuisine has vegetarian and meat varieties, though the vegetarian version remains most popular.

cover.altText: Gabacai, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Swabian beef stew named for Gaisburg, a Stuttgart district: cubed meat cooked in strong beef broth, served with potatoes and Spätzle, covered with broth, and topped with butter-fried golden-brown onions.

cover.altText: Gaisburger Marsch, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Spanish bread from Galicia made with native soft wheat flour, other wheat flour, water, sourdough, yeast, and salt. Its high hydration and long fermentation create an airy, slightly acidic crumb beneath a crisp, golden-brown crust.

cover.altText: Galician bread: Hogaza de pan gallego

list.shortDescription: A French one-pot dish of mainly root vegetables and one or more meats, slowly oven-cooked in an earthenware dish. Sometimes its cooking liquid is served as soup before the vegetables and meat as a main course.

cover.altText: Garbure: Garbure des Landes, au confit de canard

list.shortDescription: An Atlantic Canadian dish made with pizza dough and cut into thin strips rather than triangular slices. Also known as garlic cheese fingers or garlies.

cover.altText: Garlic fingers, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A South African submarine sandwich from Cape Town, made with a large bread roll filled with chips, a choice of fillings, and sauces. It is popular throughout the Western Cape and typically shared by several people.

cover.altText: Gatsby, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: Gbegiri is a bean soup associated with Nigeria’s Yoruba people, and it is commonly eaten alongside Amala or Ewedu.

cover.altText: Gbegiri: A Yoruba dish which consist of yam flour for the swallow and beans soup

list.shortDescription: A Sicilian watermelon jelly pudding served throughout summer and traditionally prepared for Ferragosto and Palermo’s Saint Rosalia celebrations.

cover.altText: Gelo di melone PAT, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: An Indonesian-Javanese cassava dish of peeled, boiled, and mashed cassava mixed with grated coconut, sugar, and a little salt. Palm sugar may replace sugar, giving the dish a brownish color and more distinctive taste.

cover.altText: Getuk: Getuk dari Magelang

list.shortDescription: A common dish from Banyumas Regency in Central Java, made from cassava—called boled by the Banyumasan people—with brown sugar, then fried for a sweet and savory result.

cover.altText: Getuk Goreng: Getuk goreng di Sokaraja

list.shortDescription: An Armenian stuffed pumpkin filled with cooked rice, butter, honey, dried fruits, nuts, and meat, then baked and usually served as dessert.

cover.altText: Ghapama, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Piedmont chocolate shaped like an ingot and wrapped in gold or silver foil, a Turin specialty named for the gianduja blend of chocolate and hazelnut.

cover.altText: Giandujotto PAT: due gianduiotti torinesi gianduiotto Torino

list.shortDescription: A traditional Kenyan meal of maize kernels and legumes boiled together with water in a sufuria, also called muthere, mutheri, or mûthekia-ngûkû.

cover.altText: Githeri: Githeri is a meal made of mostly maize and beans. It is a staple of many communities in Kenya

list.shortDescription: A Sicilian and Calabrian Christmas nougat of sesame seeds set in honey and caramelized sugar, sometimes enriched with almonds and candied orange peel and cut into diamonds or rectangles.

cover.altText: Giurgiulena, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: Beef tripe and rice form this Filipino lugaw, which is cooked with ginger and finished with toasted garlic, scallions, black pepper, and chicharon. Calamansi, soy sauce, fish sauce, or a hard-boiled egg accompanies it.

cover.altText: Goto: Goto beef Cuisine of the Philippines

list.shortDescription: A Sicilian sorbet made from sugar syrup flavored with lemon, coffee, or fruit juice, stirred as it freezes into tiny ice crystals. It is chunkier in Palermo and western Sicily than in the east.

cover.altText: Granita PAT: Granita originelle au citron de Sicile et son aspect de neige

list.shortDescription: A Greek salad combining tomatoes, cucumbers, onion, feta cheese, and olives with salt, oregano, and olive oil. Lemon juice, green bell pepper, caper berries, and mint or parsley may also be added.

cover.altText: Greek salad: Greek salad (horiatiki salata). At Psaropoulo restaurant, Hydra, Hydra

list.shortDescription: A delicacy in the cuisines of the Azores and Madeira, made with seasoned limpets grilled in their shells and usually eaten as an appetizer. Patella aspera and Patella candei are the species most commonly used.
A Mexican street-food sandwich common in Mexico City and the State of Mexico, with a tamal tucked inside a bolillo or round telera.

cover.altText: Guajolota: Torta de Tamal, conocida como Guajolota

list.shortDescription: A Caltanissetta, Sicily, dessert of soft wheat flour fried in lard and brushed with melted honey, also used as the folded pastry around ricotta filling for raviola di ricotta nissena.

cover.altText: Guastedda dolce nissena: Guasteddra dolce di Caltanissetta

list.shortDescription: A traditional Indian sweet made in different regions and popular in marketplaces. Rural versions are prepared for specific festive occasions in Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Punjab, Odisha, Haryana, and Rajasthan.

cover.altText: Gulgula: Golden fried blobs made with a batter of flour and brown sugar

list.shortDescription: A northern Nigerian bread from Kano State with a lighter dough than ordinary bread, eaten for breakfast, lunch, or as a snack.

cover.altText: Gurasa, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A rich, aromatic Kashmiri meatball curry made with finely minced mutton, yogurt, and spices, served as the final course of the traditional multi-course wazwan feast.

cover.altText: Gushtab, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: Australian halal snack packs combine halal-certified doner kebab meat with chips and sauces, with yoghurt, cheese, jalapeños, or tabbouleh added. Traditionally served in polystyrene, they now commonly use moulded pulp or cardboard containers.

cover.altText: Halal snack pack: A photo of a halal snack pack

list.shortDescription: A Syrian dessert of semolina and cheese dough filled with qishta. Associated with central Syria, it is also found in Tripoli and Lebanon, with Syrian immigrants carrying it to Turkey and Germany.

cover.altText: Halawet el Jibn: حلاوة الجبن الحموية

list.shortDescription: A flat, round bread popular in Chile and Bolivia, baked with wheat flour, yeast, sugar, salt, milk, water, and vegetable or sometimes animal shortening, and used for traditional sandwiches.

cover.altText: Hallulla: two typically Chilean breads: hallulla (left) and marraqueta (right)

list.shortDescription: A white surimi product from Japan with a soft, mild taste, made in square, triangular, or round forms. Believed to have been created by Hanpei of Suruga during the Edo period, it is used in oden, soups, and stews, or fried and broiled.

cover.altText: Hampen, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Cambodian pizza made with cannabis-infused ingredients containing enough THC to produce psychoactive effects.
A traditional North African soup prepared in Morocco and Algeria, harira is popular as a starter or a light snack on its own. It is served mostly during Ramadan but can be made year-round.

cover.altText: Harira: Soupe traditionnelle du Maroc servie surtout pendant le jeûne du mois sacré de Ramadan

list.shortDescription: A Canadian pizza topped with pineapple, tomato sauce, mozzarella, and either ham or bacon. Sam Panopoulos created the first at the Satellite Restaurant in Chatham-Kent, Ontario, in 1962.

cover.altText: Hawaiian pizza: Pizza with ham and pineapple: Boston's North End Pizza Bakery Oahu, Hawai'i

list.shortDescription: A French dish pairing fried chicken with a sauce of mushrooms, onions or shallots, tomatoes, and wine, sometimes with stock and assorted herbs.

cover.altText: Hunter's chicken: Pollo alla cacciatora (hunter's chicken)

list.shortDescription: Iceland’s national dish is fermented Greenland shark or other sleeper shark, cured by fermentation and hung to dry for four to five months. Its strong ammonia-rich smell and fishy taste make it an acquired taste.

cover.altText: Hákarl: Hákarl (Icelandic for shark) or Greenlandic Shark is a food from Iceland. This picture was taken near Bjarnahöfn in 2005

list.shortDescription: A Portuguese chocolate salami dessert made with cocoa, chocolate, broken biscuits, and butter, sometimes including port wine or rum.

cover.altText: Salame turco PAT: Chocolat Salami

list.shortDescription: A Peruvian street-food sandwich common in Lima, made with specially prepared pork called “country ham,” salsa criolla, and lettuce in French bread or a rosette.

cover.altText: butifarra: Before heading to the house we had to make a stop at the Queirolo wich sold a delicious butifarra sandwich

list.shortDescription: An Italian dish of braised chicken or rabbit with onions, herbs, and usually tomatoes, often with peppers and sometimes wine. Its preparation varies by region, and some versions include mushrooms.

cover.altText: cacciatore, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A French cold dessert of lightly sweetened coffee, coffee-flavoured ice cream, and Chantilly cream, assembled in a large glass just before serving and topped with crushed roasted coffee beans.

cover.altText: café liégeois: Café liégeois

list.shortDescription: A Flemish beef stew popular in Belgium, the Netherlands, and French Flanders, made with beer and mustard, with bread sometimes used to thicken the sauce.

cover.altText: carbonade flamande: Carbonade flamande

list.shortDescription: A pasta dish from Lazio, Italy, combining cured pork, hard cheese, eggs, salt, and black pepper. Its modern form and name emerged in the mid-20th century.

cover.altText: carbonara: Plato de espaguetis con la salsa carbonara tradicional, hecha a base de huevo, guanciale de cerdo y queso pecorino romano

list.shortDescription: A Toledo specialty served as a tapa, made with lean pork stewed in moderately spicy tomato sauce with peas, and served in an earthenware casserole with potatoes and bread.

cover.altText: carcamusa: Carcamusas, a spanish dish from Toledo

list.shortDescription: A Sicilian dessert from Agira in Enna, found throughout the province and much of eastern Sicily. It is officially recognized among Italy’s traditional agri-food products.

cover.altText: cassatella di Agira: Cassatelle di Agira, typical Sicilian sweet

list.shortDescription: An Italian autumnal chestnut flour cake made with water, olive oil, pine nuts, and raisins, then baked. In Livorno, a 3-centimeter-thick version is called toppone.

cover.altText: castagnaccio: Castagnaccio with pine nuts and sultanas

list.shortDescription: An American marinated celery salad dating to 1910 and devised by Victor Hirtzler, head chef at San Francisco’s St. Francis Hotel. Hirtzler is also credited with inventing Crab Louie.

cover.altText: celery Victor: Cathy2's Celery Victor -- celery braised in chicken stock with a vinaigrette dressing (from when Celery was King!)

list.shortDescription: Ceviche is Peru’s national dish: a cold dish of raw fish or shellfish marinated in citrus and seasonings, recognized by UNESCO as Peruvian traditional cuisine.

cover.altText: ceviche, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A South African vegetable relish, usually spicy, served with bread, pap, samp, stews, or curries. It reportedly developed among Mozambican mineworkers near Johannesburg from tinned produce with chili in a Portuguese style.

cover.altText: chakalaka: Chakalaka

list.shortDescription: A Nagasaki noodle dish of pork, seafood, and vegetables fried with lard, combined with chicken-and-pig-bone broth and boiled with specially made ramen noodles in one pan.

cover.altText: champon: A bowl of champon noodles at the Chinese restaurant "Shikairo" in Nagasaki, Japan

list.shortDescription: An Indian chickpea curry cooked in a tomato-based sauce and served with bread, including deep-fried bhatura, puri, or flatbreads such as kulcha. It is also a staple in Pakistani cuisine.

cover.altText: chana masala: Picture of chana (chick peas) masala at Le Taj restaurant. Channa masala

list.shortDescription: A Pakistani kebab of minced beef, mutton, or chicken shaped into a patty and seasoned with spices, associated with Pashtun cuisine and prepared across South Asia.

cover.altText: chapli kebab: Chapli Kebab served in a Birmingham Balti restaurant

list.shortDescription: Meat fried and then stewed with tomatoes is the basis of this Georgian dish. It counts among Georgian cuisine’s main meat dishes but is less familiar abroad than Satsivi or Chakhokhbili.

cover.altText: chashushuli: A dish of Chashushuli (Georgian spicy beef stew), bread and Georgian-style salad, along with a glass of water, served at restaurant Rioni in Haukilahti, Espoo, Finland

list.shortDescription: A French apple turnover filled with applesauce, named since the 18th century after the method used to fill the viennoiserie dough. A lemon-cream-filled version is called a chausson au citron.

cover.altText: chausson aux pommes: Chaussons aux pommes fabriqués artisanalement au four banal de la Pannevert par le Centre d’Histoire Sociale de Haute-Normandie

list.shortDescription: A Japanese savoury egg custard seasoned with soy sauce, dashi and mirin, with shiitake, kamaboko, yuri-ne, ginkgo and boiled shrimp in a tea-cup-like container, eaten with a spoon.

cover.altText: chawanmushi: Chawan-mushi in a restaurant in Hamamatsu, Japan

list.shortDescription: A popular British meal made by placing sliced or grated cheese on toasted bread and melting it under a grill.

cover.altText: cheese on toast: A plate of cheese on toast

list.shortDescription: A United States baked good of bread dough enclosing melted cheese: a Yakima version baked in squares and a Concord version shaped into crimped circles to keep the cheese inside.
Chelow kabab, Iran’s national dish, pairs steamed rice with a variety of Iranian kebab and was probably created during the Qajar dynasty.

cover.altText: chelow kabab: Bakhtyari (above), an Iranian form of kebab

list.shortDescription: A Malaysian adaptation of fried and grilled chicken, invented by Hainanese migrant workers during colonial Malaya and often found in kopitiams and Hainanese or western restaurants.

cover.altText: chicken chop: Chicken Chops and Chips at Red Tea House Original caption: Piter wanted chicken chops! mmm... gravy + chips! 红茶古 Red Tea House Kuantan, Malaysia

list.shortDescription: An Irish deli roll of processed chicken fillet in a baguette, sold throughout Ireland in convenience shops, supermarkets, petrol stations, fast-food restaurants, and casual eateries.

cover.altText: chicken fillet roll: A photograph of an Irish chicken fillet baguette bought from a Spar deli on Liffey Street in Dublin

list.shortDescription: A Visayan chicken dish marinated in calamansi, black pepper, coconut vinegar, and annatto, grilled over hot coals and basted with the marinade. It is served with rice, calamansi, soy sauce, chicken oil, and vinegar.

cover.altText: chicken inasal: © Michael Reyes

list.shortDescription: An American dish of diced, shredded, or sliced chicken in a cream sauce, with mushrooms, pimientos, and sherry in the usual version. It accompanied toast points or filled pastry cases, and later was served with rice or noodles.

cover.altText: chicken à la King: Chicken à la King over noodles

list.shortDescription: A Mexican spicy stew of chili peppers, usually beef, tomatoes, and beans, seasoned with garlic, onions, and cumin.

cover.altText: chili: Bowl of Chili con Carne, made of ground pork, cubed beef, beans, tomatoes and hot peppers. Decorated with two Tortilla chips

list.shortDescription: A Chinese dish of stir-fried shrimp in chili sauce, prepared in Sichuan and Shanghai styles. The Sichuan version uses dried chilies, onions, and tomatoes for crisp texture.

cover.altText: chili shrimp: Ebi chili

list.shortDescription: A Belizean dish common in Yucatán and Belize, made with spices and pieces of black recado, an achiote paste. Known as Black Dinner for its dark appearance, most Belizeans make it at home and for special occasions.

cover.altText: chimole: Chicken thigh in red mole sauce served with rice. At a restaurant in Taxco de Alarcón, Guerrero, Mexico

list.shortDescription: An American Christmas cookie created by Helen Fredell of Saint Paul, Minnesota, with a crisp powdered-sugar exterior and chewy, brownie-like center. It is made with cocoa powder or chocolate.

cover.altText: chocolate crinkle: Pictured above is a plate of chocolate cookies with powdered sugar on top

list.shortDescription: Chraime is a spicy North African stew of fish and tomatoes. Jews traditionally eat it on Erev Shabbat, Rosh Hashanah, and at Passover seders; its name comes from the Arabic word for “hot.”

cover.altText: chraime: צלחת חריימה של סבתא שלי (גמילה זנזורי) שהכינה לליל הסדר 2017

list.shortDescription: A Korean tang (soup) featuring pond loach, a freshwater fish. Namwon in southwestern South Korea is known for its version.

cover.altText: chueo-tang: Chueotang. A Korean fish dish. (Gangjin, Jeollanam-do, South Korea)

list.shortDescription: Brazilian churrasco is grilled beef, known by a Portuguese and Spanish term also used for varied meat products across South America and Iberia.

cover.altText: churrasco: Churrasco

list.shortDescription: A Vietnamese dessert of glutinous rice filled with mung bean paste, bathed in ginger syrup, warmed, and garnished with sesame seeds and coconut milk. It is served during Lunar New Year and the Cold-Eating Festival.

cover.altText: chè trôi nước, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Hanoi grilled-fish delicacy: hemibagrus catfish marinated with turmeric, galangal, and fermented rice, then charcoal-grilled and eaten with scallion, dill, bún noodles, herbs, peanuts, and mắm tôm.

cover.altText: chả cá Lã Vọng: Chả cá Lã Vọng Hà Nội

list.shortDescription: A Vietnamese steamed egg-and-pork meat loaf, usually served with hot rice, cucumber, and chili sauce.
Ciccioli are Italian cakes of fatty pork pressed into shape. Across Emilia-Romagna, they are popular in Modena, Reggio Emilia, Bologna, Parma, Piacenza, and Romagna.

cover.altText: ciccioli: This is a plate of ciccioli, which are like pork rinds

list.shortDescription: A sweet roll common in Northern Europe and North America. Some versions use puff pastry rather than yeasted dough, with both prepared by much the same method.

cover.altText: cinnamon roll: Cinnamon roll in Stockholm

list.shortDescription: A Turkish kebab of skewered liver associated with Diyarbakır, usually served with sliced onions, salad, and bread and often eaten for breakfast in Diyarbakır and Gaziantep.

cover.altText: ciğer kebap, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: Three bread slices are layered with poultry, fried bacon strips, lettuce, tomato, and mayonnaise. The sandwich is often cut diagonally into quarters or halves and kept together with cocktail sticks.

cover.altText: club sandwich: A club sandwich containing chicken and ham between four layers of bread, served at Café Picnic at the Forum shopping centre in Kamppi, Helsinki, Finland

list.shortDescription: An American fruit or savory filling baked in a large dish under a topping of batter, biscuits, or dumplings.

cover.altText: cobbler: And made a delicious cobbler using one of the duck eggs from Dog Mountain

list.shortDescription: A traditional stew eaten as a main course in Spain, Portugal, Brazil, and other Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking countries.

cover.altText: cocido: Cozido de grão, a typical portuguese dish, photographed in the city of Beja

list.shortDescription: A Canadian cod bake from Newfoundland, covered in creamy white béchamel sauce and topped with cheese that browns into a crust.
