list.shortDescription: A Filipino scrambled egg dish from the Ilocos Region of northwestern Luzon, made with roasted eggplant, garlic, onions, tomatoes, eggs, and fermented fish sauce. Commonly served with steamed rice or alongside grilled meat or fish.

cover.altText: Poqui poqui: A. Heritage and people 2. Cuisine and delicacies

list.shortDescription: A Finnish carrot casserole of mashed carrots, boiled rice or barley, and liquid, usually milk or cream, then baked in the oven. It is eaten mostly at Christmas.

cover.altText: Porkkanalaatikko: Porkkanalaatikko

list.shortDescription: An Iranian fast-food sausage sold in sandwich shops as a sub or meal, made with onion, tomato paste, ground chilli pepper, and spices. It is common in Khuzestan province, where it is very hot and spicy.

cover.altText: Port sausage, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A French-Flemish potted-meat dish combining three or four meats with natural gelatin, sliced onions, salt, pepper, thyme, and bay leaves. It is slow-cooked for three hours, chilled, served cold, and customarily topped with chips.

cover.altText: Potjevleesch: Potjevleesch

list.shortDescription: French pralines are firm sweets combining almonds or hazelnuts with caramelized sugar. Cream is also a common ingredient in pralines.

cover.altText: Praline, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Polish potato dish from Poręba: sliced or diced potatoes braised with lard, onions, and kiełbasa, or with beets and carrots, covered with cabbage, tightly sealed in a special container, and served with kefir and mizeria.

cover.altText: Prażonki: Pieczonki - Polish local dish from Zaglembia

list.shortDescription: A Japanese snack made by Ezaki Glico, shaped as a stick with a pretzel-like texture and dusted with seasonings rather than coated in flavoured fudge.

cover.altText: Pretz: The roast (red) and salad (green) varieties of Pretz, created by Ezaki Glico

list.shortDescription: A traditional Newar delicacy from Nepal’s Kathmandu Valley, Pukālā features boiled and fried water-buffalo meats and is served at wedding and festival feasts, after the main course and before dessert.
A Mangalorean rice dumpling from Tulu Nadu, made by soaking, grinding, tempering, cooking, and steaming rice. Called Pundi Gatti in Udupi and Mangalore, it is usually served with coconut chutney.

cover.altText: Pundi: Pundi - The Rice Dumpling Food Item from TuluNadu, India

list.shortDescription: A Banjarese dish from South Kalimantan, Indonesia, combining steamed rice, coconut milk, and sambal habang in a banana-leaf parcel that is steamed.

cover.altText: Pundut nasi, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A dense Filipino bread roll made with all-purpose flour, milk, and salt, usually coated in coarse white sugar. A cross-cut before baking creates its crown-like, star-shaped top.

cover.altText: Putok: Putok bread (Philippines), a variant of pan de monja (monay)

list.shortDescription: A Singaporean kueh and sweet snack of steamed rice flour, molded into a flower shape and filled with palm sugar. It is a traditional dessert among Singapore’s Malay community.
A green Chinese dumpling from Jiangnan, made with glutinous rice and Chinese mugwort or barley grass and usually filled with sweet red or black bean paste.

cover.altText: Qingtuan: Qingtuan, traditional Chinese food of the Qingming festival

list.shortDescription: A dense pudding from Cantabria, Spain, made with milk, sugar, butter, wheat flour, and egg, flavored with lemon zest and cinnamon, and served hot or cold.

cover.altText: Quesada Pasiega: Quesadas, a typical dessert of Cantabria (Spain)

list.shortDescription: A thick soup from Gaspésie and elsewhere in Maritime Quebec, flavored with salting-cod residues and thickened with flour. Recipes may add bacon, potatoes, turnips, onions, milk, cream, turbot, sturgeon, or salmon.

cover.altText: Quiaude: Traditionnal Gaspesian turbot stew

list.shortDescription: Brazilian baked custard with Portuguese heritage, made chiefly from sugar, egg yolks and ground coconut. Usually presented in an upturned cup with a glistening surface; a ring-mold version, quindão, is served in slices.

cover.altText: Quindim: Photo of a Quindim (Brazilian sweet)

list.shortDescription: A Mexican dish of sliced poblano peppers and onions, sautéed and simmered with cream; chicken broth is sometimes added. It is popular in central and southern Mexico and commonly served at taquizas.

cover.altText: Rajas con crema: Mexican dish, Rajas con crema

list.shortDescription: A layered Hungarian casserole of sliced potatoes, sour cream, smoked sausage, and hard-boiled eggs, served at luncheon, as a main course, or as a side dish.

cover.altText: Rakott krumpli: Rakott krumpli - a Hungarian dish made of layered potato with eggs, bacon and sausage

list.shortDescription: A Turkish bread made from wheat flour and yeast, round and flat with a weave-like patterned crust, topped with sesame and Nigella sativa seeds and often egg-washed, and served at iftar and sahur during Ramadan.

cover.altText: Ramadan pide: "Ramazan pidesi", not from a traditional bakery but put to oven in a supermarket. Ramadan 2016 in Turkey

list.shortDescription: A South Indian breakfast variation of idli made with coarse-ground wheat or rice rava, semolina, or Bombay rava. This Karnataka specialty is served hot with saagu and coconut chutney, with ghee poured over it.

cover.altText: Rava idli: Rava Idli

list.shortDescription: Tiny ravioli associated with Dauphiné in South-Central France, particularly around Romans-sur-Isère, enclose Comté or Emmental, faisselle, butter and parsley between two soft-wheat pasta layers made with eggs and water.
An emblematic Louisiana Creole dish of small red beans, vegetables, spices, and pork bones slowly cooked together and served over rice, traditionally prepared on Mondays.

cover.altText: Red beans and rice: This a picture of a plate of red beans and rice from the Chimes Restaurant in Baton Rouge, Louisiana

list.shortDescription: A Yucatán, Mexico, dish of turkey and ground pork mixed with chilies, tomato, achiote, garlic, spices, and boiled eggs, traditionally prepared in November for the Hanal Pixán festival.

cover.altText: Relleno Negro: Pavo Relleno Negro, turkey in a black sauce from the Yucatan

list.shortDescription: An Argentine hash of fried julienned potatoes, ham and eggs, sometimes made with peas, fresh vegetables, fish, pork or other meats. It is common in Buenos Aires, and French fries may also be used.

cover.altText: Revuelto Gramajo: Revuelto Gramajo. Argentina

list.shortDescription: A Swiss risotto from Ticino, made with short-grain rice roasted in oil and slowly cooked in broth with regional Merlot, butter, grated cheese and often mushrooms, then served with luganighe sausage.

cover.altText: Risotto alla ticinese: Dish served at the Locanda Barbarossa (Ascona): Locally cultivated Loto Risotto, green asparagus, white Merlot, Piora alpine cheese

list.shortDescription: An aromatic curried meat dish in Kashmiri cuisine, made with mutton or goat and colored and flavored by alkanet flower and Kashmiri chillies. Tomatoes are often used in the West instead.

cover.altText: Rogan josh: Rogan Josh Kashmiri

list.shortDescription: A dessert from the Nisseno area, produced by local pastry chefs and eaten year-round, without being tied to any particular event or occasion.

cover.altText: Rollò: Rollò nisseno tipo mignon

list.shortDescription: Madagascar’s national dish is a stew of greens, zebu meat, tomatoes, and onions, usually served with rice. It includes brèdes mafana, or anamalaho, whose buds produce a tingly, pungent, citrusy, mouth-numbing effect and stimulate abundant salivation.

cover.altText: Romazava: Romanzawa - Madagaskar Stew mit Hühnchen und Rind, grünen Auberginen und als Gewürz Jambu (Acmella oleracea) dazu roter Reis

list.shortDescription: A traditional Brazilian dessert pairing a slice of cheese with goiabada, or combining both in other preparations. Named for Romeo and Juliet, it casts cheese as Romeu and goiabada as Julieta.

cover.altText: Romeu and Julieta: Romeo e Julieta (esquerda) e doce de leite (direita), doces típicos de Minas Gerais

list.shortDescription: A Betawi bread from Indonesia, made in two sweetened pieces shaped like a crocodile and always present at traditional Betawi wedding ceremonies.

cover.altText: Roti buaya: Roti Buaya or "Crocodile Bread", is Betawi (native Jakartans) delicacy of crocodile shaped bread. It is often served in festive occassions such as weddings and celebrative moments. Jakarta, Indonesia

list.shortDescription: A Singaporean street-food omelette sandwich dating to the 1960s: a baguette-like loaf halved and griddled with beaten egg, onions, and minced lamb, sardines, or chicken.

cover.altText: Roti john: Roti John - served

list.shortDescription: A Thai dessert with Indian Muslim influence: silky spun-sugar floss wrapped in very thin roti made from white, colored, or pandan-green flour and sprinkled with sesame.

cover.altText: Roti sai mai, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A rich, slightly sweet Bengali dish possibly from Old Dhaka, Bangladesh, shaped by Mughal-era Mughlai cuisine and known for its many spices and ingredients, with several regional variants.

An early scientific-nutrition soup devised by Benjamin Thompson, Reichsgraf von Rumford, around 1800 and eaten in Munich and greater Bavaria. It was used to feed the poor, workhouses, military workhouses, and prisoners.

cover.altText: Rumford's Soup, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Jamaican and Tobagonian stew, also known as run dun, rondón, fling-me-far, or fling mi for, eaten in several Latin American countries sharing a coast with the Caribbean Sea.

cover.altText: Run down: A plate of rondon

list.shortDescription: In Greek cuisine, saganaki covers several dishes prepared in a small frying pan, best known as an appetizer of fried cheese and often flambéed in North America.

cover.altText: Saganaki: Saganaki

list.shortDescription: Japanese hard candies flavored with fruit juice and sold in collectible tins with frequently changing designs. Available since 1908, they have become a recognizable icon in Japan.

cover.altText: Sakuma drops: Sakuma shiki drops (Candy)

list.shortDescription: An American meat dish made from ground beef blended with chicken, pork, and other ingredients, often served with brown-sauce-like gravy, mashed potatoes, and cooked vegetables.

cover.altText: Salisbury steak: Two salisbury steaks with brown sauce

list.shortDescription: A Waray pancake from Eastern Samar made with galapong, coconut milk, sugar, and water. Tubâ or yeast leavens it before it is pan-fried or cooked in a greased clay pot, often for breakfast or merienda.

cover.altText: Salukara, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A chilli-based sauce or paste in Indonesian cuisine, part of a sambal tradition found across maritime Southeast Asia and, through migration, South Africa, Suriname, and the Netherlands.

cover.altText: Sambal tuktuk: Sambal untuk ikan bakar

list.shortDescription: An instant noodle brand from South Korea, Samyang Ramen was launched by Samyang Foods on 15 September 1963 as the country’s first ramen product. Company chairman Jeong Jung-yun created it.

cover.altText: Samyang Ramen: Instant ramen of Samyang Foods <Samyang Ramen>

list.shortDescription: A savory, spicy Indonesian dish of the Batak people, prepared by stewing minced pork or dog meat in blood with coconut milk, kaffir lime, garlic, chilies, Thai pepper, lemongrass, ginger, turmeric, and andaliman.

cover.altText: Sangsang: Batak cuisine, the saksang pork stew cooked in its blood and spices

list.shortDescription: A Chinese Indonesian tofu dish prepared and served in a claypot, in vegetarian form or with chicken, seafood, minced beef, or pork.

cover.altText: Sapo tahu: Seafood and tofu claypot ( sapo ). Tastes better than it looks..., Bintan

list.shortDescription: An Italian antipasto of fried sardines with sweet-and-sour onions, pine nuts, and raisins, typical of Venetian cuisine. This cicchetto is often served as a snack in Venetian bacari.

cover.altText: Sarde in saor PAT: Sarde in saor dans un restaurant vénitien (décembre 2022)

list.shortDescription: A cheeseless pizza from Liguria, Italy, similar to the pissaladière and considered by some closer to focaccia. It is named for Admiral Andrea Doria, whose favorite was bread with olive oil, garlic, and salted anchovy.
A traditional Canadian fruit pie with saskatoon berry filling, particularly associated with Saskatchewan. It is often served with whipped cream, ice cream, or slices of cheddar cheese.

cover.altText: Saskatoon berry pie: Berry, berry good

list.shortDescription: A specialty satay of Gorontalese cuisine in Sulawesi, Indonesia, established by the Gorontalese in the early 19th century and popular for its skipjack tuna from the Sulawesi Sea and Gulf of Tomini.

cover.altText: Satay Tuna, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Palatinate specialty whose meat-like stomach forms the casing, packed with filling and finished by pan-frying or roasting until crisp.

cover.altText: Saumagen: Saumagen mit Sauerkraut, ein typisches Gericht der Pfälzer Küche

list.shortDescription: A Filipino sweet rice cake steamed in cone-shaped banana leaves, found in northeastern Mindanao, Bohol, Eastern Visayas, and the Bicol Region.

A Sicilian stuffed flatbread made with thin rectangular dough folded three or four times, filled with ricotta and onion, cheese and tomato, tomato and onion, or tomato and eggplant, and eaten hot or cold.

cover.altText: Scacciata PAT: Typical Sicilian food

list.shortDescription: A Scottish soup of barley, lamb, mutton or beef, root vegetables and dried pulses, with cabbage and leeks often added shortly before serving. Recipes vary, and it has long been sold ready-prepared in tins.

cover.altText: Scotch broth: lunch at Inveraray Castle - Scotch broth

list.shortDescription: A meat stew with potatoes, carrots, and onions, particularly associated with Liverpool. The name derives from lobscouse, a dish of meat and ships biscuit eaten by Northern European sailors.

cover.altText: Scouse: Scouse, Lobby, or Lobscouse

list.shortDescription: Indonesian smoked meat from Rote Island, popular in Kupang, East Nusa Tenggara. It may be made from pork, beef, or game such as venison, though pork is now the most popular.

cover.altText: Se'i: Se'i babi, smoked pork, specialty of Kupang city, East Nusa Tenggara, Indonesia

list.shortDescription: A pizza topped primarily with seafood, which may be fresh, frozen, or canned. Some retail pizza chains and smaller restaurants offer it.

cover.altText: Seafood pizza: 海鮮トマトピッツァ

list.shortDescription: A Sardinian deep-fried semolina-and-lard dumpling filled with soured Pecorino Sardo and lemon peel, covered with honey, sugar, and sometimes salt.

cover.altText: Sebada: Seadas; traditional sardinian dessert

list.shortDescription: A spicy Sundanese dish from Bandung, West Java, made with kurupuk soaked in a broth cooked with protein sources. It is sold at restaurants, warungs, and street carts.

cover.altText: Seblak: Seblak di Garut, Jawa Barat

list.shortDescription: Sekba, also called bektim, is a Chinese Indonesian pork-offal stew in a mildly sweet and salty soy sauce-based soup seasoned with garlic and Chinese herbs, served as street food in Jakarta’s Chinatowns.

cover.altText: Sekba, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Javanese specialty from Solo, Central Java, featuring braised beef tenderloin in a thin sauce of garlic, vinegar, kecap manis, Worcestershire sauce, nutmeg, and black pepper, served with egg, vegetables, and potato chips.

cover.altText: Selat Solo, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A traditional Bali–Java pancake-like snack made with rice flour batter, coconut milk or cream, and shredded coconut, usually served with kinca, a golden-brown coconut sugar syrup.

cover.altText: Serabi: Serabi is made from flour mix coconut milk and javanese sugar, baked with tembikar in a smal pan. It taste so good for snacking or breakfast

list.shortDescription: A Javanese side dish and condiment made from spiced grated coconut, served with rice in Indonesia. Recipes may be sweet or hot and spicy.

cover.altText: Serundeng: Serundeng Daging, fried beef in sauteed grated coconut and spices. Javanese cuisine, Indonesia

list.shortDescription: A Sicilian pizza popular in western Sicily by the mid-19th century and the region’s usual pizza until the 1860s. It later reached North America with a thicker crust and rectangular shape.

cover.altText: Sfincione PAT, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: An Indian stew of slow-cooked turnip and mutton associated with the Kashmir Valley and Mughlai cuisine, left to simmer overnight. In Persian, “shab” means “night” and “daig” means “cooking pot.”

cover.altText: Shab Deg: Shab Daigg

list.shortDescription: A ceremonial wedding platter in Bangladesh’s Muslim community, lavishly arranged for the groom with whole roasted goat or chicken, polao or biryani, kebab, rezala, korma, and eggs, and decorated with carved fruit and vegetable salad.

cover.altText: Shagorana: A Shagorana platter served at a Bangladeshi wedding featuring a whole roasted goat, lobsters, chicken roasts, eggs, aromatic polao, and decorative cut salads

list.shortDescription: A Central Asian salad of thinly sliced tomatoes and onions seasoned with salt and black pepper, popular in Tajikistan, Uzbekistan, and Kyrgyzstan.

cover.altText: Shakarap: Shakarab/shakarob, a simple salad from Central Asia

list.shortDescription: Shakriyeh, also known as laban emmo, is a traditional Levantine stew made with lamb and yogurt and often served alongside Arabic rice.

cover.altText: Shakriyeh, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Seychellois fish dish of boiled, skinned shark, finely mashed and cooked with bilimbi juice, lime, onion, pepper, salt, turmeric, and oil.

cover.altText: Shark chutney: Meal served in Mahé, Seychelles on October 20, 2010, consisting of shark chutney, lentils, and shredded green papaya on rice

list.shortDescription: An Azerbaijani dessert from the Sheki region, also called Sheki pakhlava. One account credits the khan’s cooks with creating it; another credits Tabriz merchant Mashadi Huseyn with spreading the recipe.

cover.altText: Sheki halva: Cuisine of Azerbaijan: Halva in Sheky style

list.shortDescription: A traditional Persian rice pilaf served for occasions such as weddings, also called Persian wedding rice or Rosh Hashanah rice. It is a simplified form of morassa' polō, meaning “jeweled rice.”

cover.altText: Shirin polo: Shirin polo, also known as Persian wedding rice

list.shortDescription: A European-style cookie made and sold by Ishiya in Sapporo, Hokkaido, with chocolate sandwiched between langue de chat. The White version uses white chocolate; the Black version uses milk chocolate.

cover.altText: Shiroi Koibito: 白い恋人（石屋製菓）

list.shortDescription: An Israeli soup accompaniment of crisp mini croutons, made as small yellow squares from flour and palm oil. Parve and suitable for meat or cream soups, they contain no almonds despite the name.

cover.altText: Shkedei marak: Shkedey Marak (Soup Almonds) - mini crisp croutons which are added to soup in Israel.שקדי מרק

list.shortDescription: A Georgian dish of fried chicken cooked over low heat in garlic sauce for 20–25 minutes and paired with bread.

cover.altText: Shkmeruli, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Georgian white-flour bread shaped like a canoe. Long strands of dough are stuck to the inside of a round brick or clay oven during baking. It is popular at Easter, Christmas, New Year’s Day, birthdays, and weddings.

cover.altText: Shoti: Georgian shoti-bread

list.shortDescription: A Kagawa specialty of parched broad beans soaked overnight in soy sauce and sugar, usually with mirin and sake, served with lunch or dinner or as an accompaniment to alcohol.

cover.altText: Shoyumame: しょうゆ豆 380g

list.shortDescription: A Louisiana Creole dish of shrimp, tomatoes, and the “holy trinity” of onion, celery, and bell pepper, seasoned with hot pepper sauce or cayenne-based seasoning and served over steamed or boiled white rice.

cover.altText: Shrimp Creole: Shrimp Creole

list.shortDescription: A traditional Ukrainian holiday flatbread made from wheat, cut into small pieces and topped with diluted honey and poppy seeds.

cover.altText: Shulyky, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Burmese dessert of glutinous rice cooked with pandan leaves, coconut milk, and jaggery, garnished with fresh coconut shavings.

cover.altText: Shwe htamin: Glutinous rice based food

list.shortDescription: Filipino ice cream made with labuyo chili, coconut milk, puréed strawberries, and sugar. Invented at the 1st Colonial Grill restaurant in Albay in 2004, it draws on Bicol’s spicy coconut-milk dishes.

cover.altText: Sili ice cream: Sili Ice Cream

list.shortDescription: A class of Filipino breakfast dishes combining sinangag and itlog, usually with a savory fried meat such as tapa, longganisa, or ham. The accompaniment supplies the combined name: tapsilog, longsilog, or hamsilog.

cover.altText: Silog: Filipino food

list.shortDescription: A Malaysian smoked-meat tradition of Sabah’s indigenous Kadazan, Dusun, Murut, and Rungus peoples, whose meat is smoked over indirect heat from firewood and charcoal.

cover.altText: Sinalau: Sinalau

list.shortDescription: A Pakistani meat-and-rice biryani from Sindh made with mutton, chicken, fish, or shrimp, basmati rice, potatoes, tomatoes, onions, spices, and yoghurt.

cover.altText: Sindhi biryani: Sindhi Biryani is a delicious Dish of Sindh

list.shortDescription: A Filipino rice dish of the Kalagan people in the Caraga and Davao regions of Mindanao, cooked with turmeric and other spices and similar to Maranao kuning and Indonesian nasi kuning.

An Indonesian steamed dumpling adapted from Chinese shumai, traditionally made with pork but often prepared with tenggiri, tuna, mackerel, prawn, or chicken and served with vegetables in peanut sauce.

cover.altText: Siomay: Siomay udang (shrimp dumpling) in a restaurant in Glodok area, Jakarta Chinatown. This dish is similar to Chinese dim sum, it is Chinese Indonesian delicacy

list.shortDescription: A Taiwanese snack sandwich of pork sausage wrapped in a sticky rice patty, usually chargrilled. Deluxe versions in Taiwanese night markets come with pickled cucumber, garlic, hot peppers, wasabi, or thick soy sauce paste.

cover.altText: Small sausage in large sausage: Small sausage in large sausage

list.shortDescription: A confection of finely shaved, fluffy ice flavored with sugar syrup that the ice absorbs, unlike the coarser, crunchier snow cone.

cover.altText: Sno-ball: Frozen dessert

list.shortDescription: A Bulgarian salad of cucumber and garlic in strained yogurt with dill, salt, and cooking oil, sometimes adding roasted peppers, walnuts, and parsley. Also known as milk or dry tarator salad.

cover.altText: Snow White salad: Snow White salad ( Snezhanka ) or dry tarator salad

list.shortDescription: An Afrikaans sweet potato dish from South Africa, baked in a Dutch oven with butter, brown sugar and cinnamon, sometimes lemon juice. It is commonly served at braais alongside snoek.

cover.altText: Soetpatats: Soetpatats, an Afrikaans dish from South Africa that includes sweet potatoes, butter, cinnamon, and brown sugar

list.shortDescription: A porridge-like rice dish from Sylhet, Bangladesh, made with aromatic rice, ghee, kalozira, fenugreek and other spices. It is a traditional Sylheti food served at dinner during Ramadan.

cover.altText: Soft Khichuri: Sylheti Iftari

list.shortDescription: A thin, deep-fried flatbread from the Mithila region of Nepal and India, made with atta or maida and cooked on a tava over direct heat with ghee or mustard oil. The Maithil community uses it as festival prasada.
Sohbat, also called Painda, is a traditional Saraiki dish of the Saraiki belt, particularly associated with Tonsa. It is served to honor guests and bring people together as a symbol of unity.

cover.altText: Sohbat: Sohbat or Painda is a traditional meat based dish from Pakistan

list.shortDescription: A Danish open sandwich of rugbrød topped with smoked herring, chives, and a raw egg yolk. Gudhjem, on Bornholm, is known for its herring smokehouses.

cover.altText: Sol over Gudhjem: Sol over Gudhjem, Bornholm (2012-07-05), by Klugschnacker in Wikipedia

list.shortDescription: An Andalusian dish of cod marinated in paprika and lemon juice, wrapped in roasted red pepper and fried. Common at Madrid tapas bars, it was noted as a popular dish after Easter in a 1905 cookbook.

cover.altText: Soldaditos de Pavía: Soldaditos de Pavia

list.shortDescription: A sharp-flavoured Scottish boiled sweet associated with Galashiels, traditionally sold loose in quarter-pound portions in paper bags.

cover.altText: Soor ploom: A bag containing soor plooms (Scots for “sour plums”), a boiled sweet from Galashiels, Scotland

list.shortDescription: An Indonesian beef or buffalo soup from Makassar, South Sulawesi, made with rich beef stock, meat and offal, rice vermicelli, fried potato patties, hard-boiled egg, and aromatic spices. It is served with steamed rice and grilled milkfish.

cover.altText: Sop saudara: Sop Saudara, a Makassar-Bugis cuisine spicy beef soup, sometimes added with offals. A specialty of Makassar city, Indonesia

list.shortDescription: A savoury pie filled with Swiss chard and onion, best known in Dalmatian Poljica between Split and Omiš. Traditionally prepared in colder months and for fasting or celebrations.

cover.altText: Soparnik: Soparnik is a traditional pastry from southern Dalmatia filled with chard

list.shortDescription: A clear, non-coconut-milk soto from West Sumatra, Indonesia, usually containing beef, onion, potatoes, and white vermicelli noodles.

cover.altText: Soto Padang: Soto Padang

list.shortDescription: A dried, flaky Chinese pastry found in several Chinese cuisines. Char siu sou is the common dim sum version, while other varieties include century egg or lotus seed paste; they are also found in Hong Kong, Singapore, and some overseas Chinatowns.

cover.altText: Sou: Char siew sou

list.shortDescription: A Minnesotan bar-snack sandwich of several minced meats with onions, tomatoes, peppers, and celery; an Italian variation adds chopped pepperoni.
An American snack from Hawaii: grilled Spam placed on or between a block of rice, wrapped in nori in the style of Japanese onigiri and seasoned with salt and shoyu.

cover.altText: Spam musubi: A plate of freshly made Spam musubi

list.shortDescription: A Greek vegetarian pilaf of long-grain rice and fresh spinach, seasoned with dill, mint, onion, salt, black pepper, and olive oil. This country dish may be served hot or cold, often with feta cheese and lemon.

cover.altText: Spanakorizo: Spanakorizo, a common Greek dish prepared with spinach, rice and flavored with herbs such as dill and/or fennel

list.shortDescription: A spice-flavoured breaded meat patty popular in Irish traditional chippers, made using a recipe developed by pork butcher Maurice Walsh in the early 1950s.
A German spiced cream cheese spread from Northern Rhenish Hesse, served as an appetizer or at gatherings with lye rolls, soft pretzels, and regional wine.

cover.altText: Spundekäs, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: Steem was an American brand of caffeinated peanut butter, sold in the United States from 2014 to 2019 and marketed as an alternative to coffee.
A Palermo street food of washed guts seasoned with parsley, onion, and other pot herbs, skewered or wrapped around a leek and grilled; in Ragusa, it is baked in a casserole and called turciniuna.

cover.altText: Stigghiola, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A popular Greek dish prepared on the spot and served for lunch or a light snack, though it may also be served cold. Known as kagianas, koskosela or menemeni.

cover.altText: Strapatsada: A quick Greek meal made from eggs scrambled in olive oil, fresh tomato puree and herbs (oregano, thyme or other). Often feta cheese is added as well

list.shortDescription: Neapolitan deep-fried sweet-dough balls, crunchy outside and light within, mixed with honey, diavulilli, cinnamon, and orange rind, then shaped into mounds or rings. Often served at Christmas, sometimes warm.

cover.altText: Struffoli: Struffoli made in the traditional way from Sorrento. Marble sized dough balls covered in honey, citrus peel and hundreds and thousands

list.shortDescription: Malta’s national dish is a rabbit stew, slow-cooked or braised with wine, tomatoes, garlic, bay leaves, cloves, salt, pepper, and vegetables.

cover.altText: Stuffat tal-fenek: Rabbit pan fried and braised with wine and garlic

list.shortDescription: A Palestinian dish of turnip pieces stuffed with minced meat, rice, and local sumac, served in tomato sauce. The pieces are fried in oil before cooking, with tahini or tamarind alternatives.

cover.altText: Stuffed Turnips: طبق محشي لفت باللحمة والرز والسماق البلدي والصلصة، وهو من الأكلات التراثية الشهية في المطبخ الفلسطيني والعربي وخاصة في فصل الشتاء

list.shortDescription: A cookie with a filling, also called a stuffed biscuit; fillings include Nutella, caramel, and peanut butter.

cover.altText: Stuffed cookie: Cuccidatti fig cookies for Christmas

list.shortDescription: A Turkish dish of mallow leaves stuffed with lamb and rice or, less commonly, rice alone, also called mallow sarma or mallow dolma. It may be served with yogurt.

cover.altText: Stuffed mallow: Greek dolmadakia made with common mallow leaves stuffed with a rice and herb mix

list.shortDescription: A South Asian halva of semolina toasted in ghee or oil, then mixed with sugar syrup, honey, or jaggery powder. It may be served at breakfast or as dessert.
