list.shortDescription: An Italian cream bun made from bread filled generously with whipped cream, typical of Roman, Marche, and Abruzzo cuisine. In Puglia and Sicily, maritozzo names a braided sweet bread instead.

cover.altText: maritozzo: Maritozzo presso Caffè delle colline, Reggio Emilia

list.shortDescription: A Mozambican dish of young cassava, pumpkin, or spinach leaves pounded in a wooden mortar and pestle, then cooked with peanuts, tomatoes, garlic, onion, and coconut milk. It is often served over rice.

cover.altText: matapa: This is an image of food from

list.shortDescription: A meat pie found in cuisines worldwide consists of pastry enclosing meat and savory ingredients. It may be baked, fried, or deep-fried, and some varieties have flaky butter-enriched crusts.

cover.altText: meat pie: Chicken and rabbit meat pie

list.shortDescription: An Iranian milk pudding made with rice, sugar, and milk, thickened with rice flour, starch, or semolina, and served as a dessert across the Middle East.

cover.altText: mehallabiyya: Mhallabiyyeh (a variation of Arabic milk pudding) decorated with pistachios and rose petals. Made with semolina seeds and rose water

list.shortDescription: A Turkish breakfast dish of eggs, tomato, green peppers, and ground black and red pepper cooked in olive oil, commonly served with bread and sometimes made with onions.

cover.altText: menemen: "Menemen" (Turkish dish whose basic ingredients are eggs and tomatoes) in a "sahan" (copper cooking pan with two handles)

list.shortDescription: A small Belgian cake of two light meringue layers joined with whipped cream, then coated in cream and chocolate shavings, sometimes topped with a candied cherry. Also found in France and some U.S. cities.

cover.altText: merveilleux: Gâteau originaire de Belgique, composé de meringue, chantilly et copeaux de chocolat

list.shortDescription: A Thai dish of deep-fried rice vermicelli with sweet-and-sour sauce, often flavored with som sa peel, a Thai citrus fruit similar to citron.

cover.altText: mi krop, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: An Indonesian noodle dish of seasoned yellow wheat noodles topped with diced chicken, drawing on Chinese culinary techniques and sold by restaurants, street stalls, and travelling vendor carts.

cover.altText: mie ayam: Chicken noodle with mushroom, picture taken in Jakarta, Indonesia

list.shortDescription: A breaded cutlet closely tied to Argentina, typically made with lean, boneless beef; versions with chicken, pork, fish, eggplant, soy beans, and chickpeas are common.

cover.altText: milanesa: Típica milanesa argentina, servida con una porción de papas fritas

list.shortDescription: A French dessert of puff pastry layered with pastry cream. Its modern form was shaped by improvements made by Marie-Antoine Carême.

cover.altText: mille-feuille: Un mille-feuille français

list.shortDescription: A festive salad of cheese, eggs, canned fish, onion, and mayonnaise, topped with crumbled boiled egg yolk to resemble mimosa flowers scattered on snow. Its popularity in the USSR produced many recipe variations.

cover.altText: mimosa salad: Mimoza salad

list.shortDescription: A pea-sized Nepali sugar confection known as Prasad Dana, Gol Dana, Nakul Dana, Makaiya Laddu, or Tarasari, offered to deities during Hindu rituals.

cover.altText: mimosa sugar ball: These 'tilguls', traditional marathi laddoos eaten on Makar Sankranti day

list.shortDescription: A Bulgarian spring dish of fresh vegetables, eggs and sirene, often finished with parsley. Some variations add garlic, scallions, eggplant, okra or carrots, while others leave out sirene or onion.

cover.altText: mish-mash: Mish-mach - a vegetarian Bulgarian dish

list.shortDescription: A Belgian sandwich commonly served at friteries and cafés, especially popular among students, and also known as an “Américain” in France’s Nord region.

cover.altText: mitraillette: A Mitraillette, a sandwich with meat, fries and sauce

list.shortDescription: A Dutch pastry made from a profiterole filled with whipped cream, topped with dark chocolate and often more whipped cream plus tangerine or pineapple.

cover.altText: moorkop: Moorkoppen

list.shortDescription: A main dish of mussels and French fries in Belgium and northern France. It is Belgium’s national dish, and its French name and Dutch equivalent both mean mussels and fries.

cover.altText: moules-frites: Moules-frites at Chez Leon in Brussels

list.shortDescription: An aubergine- or potato-based dish common in the Balkans and Middle East, often made with ground meat and differing in local and regional versions.

cover.altText: moussaka, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A cold Swiss breakfast cereal prepared without cooking, developed around 1900 by physician Maximilian Bircher-Benner for hospital patients and also eaten at supper with café complet.

cover.altText: muesli, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A round Sicilian sesame bread and sandwich created by a Sicilian immigrant in the United States and popularized in New Orleans.

cover.altText: muffuletta: A collage of Central Grocery's Muffaletta in New Orleans, Louisiana. Contributed by Jason Perlow of OffTheBroiler.com

list.shortDescription: A Colombian soup from Boyacá and Santander, made with pork parts, corn, and vegetables in Santander, or more commonly beef and potato in Boyacá. Goat meat may also be used.

cover.altText: mute: Plato típico

list.shortDescription: A Turkish zucchini fritter made with grated courgette and a batter of eggs, onion, dill, parsley, and flour, sometimes with potato and cheese, then pan-fried in oil.

cover.altText: mücver: Kabak mücveri

list.shortDescription: A traditional Indonesian steamed cake from Javanese cuisine, made with rice flour, coconut milk, and sugar, filled with banana and wrapped in banana leaves.

cover.altText: nagasari: indonesian food

list.shortDescription: A Korean vegetable dish of edible greens or leaves, including wild san-namul and spring bom-namul. Boreum-namul accompanies five-grain rice on Daeboreum, the year’s first full moon.

cover.altText: namul: Ariang-themed concert at the Nokjiwon Garden of Cheong Wa Dae

list.shortDescription: An Indonesian rice dish from Tegal, Central Java, steamed in banana leaves with fried shallots and sides such as chicken curry, shredded meat, sambal, boiled eggs, spiced coconut, tempeh, and string beans.

cover.altText: nasi bogana: Nasi Bogan Picture

list.shortDescription: An Indonesian pilaf of rice cooked in goat-meat broth, goat milk, and clarified butter. It is favored by Indonesia’s Arab community and reflects Yemeni Arabian, Indian, and Afghan culinary influences.

cover.altText: nasi kebuli: Nasi Kebuli

list.shortDescription: An Indonesian rice dish from Central Java, especially Yogyakarta, Semarang, and Surakarta, with rice topped by sambal, dried fish, and tempeh and wrapped in banana leaves.

cover.altText: nasi kucing: Indonesian food

list.shortDescription: An Indonesian fragrant rice dish cooked with coconut milk and turmeric, giving nasi kuning its name. It is also found in Malaysia, Brunei, Singapore, and Cocos Island, Australia.

cover.altText: nasi kuning, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Malaysian rice dish from northern Peninsular Malaysia, prepared with the herb Vitex trifolia, locally known as lemuni.

cover.altText: nasi lemuni: Nasi Lemuni

list.shortDescription: Indonesian and Malay rice dish of cooked rice with ghee and spices, traditionally served at weddings, kenduri, religious celebrations, and other ceremonies across Sumatra, the Malay Peninsula, Singapore, southern Thailand, and the Riau Archipelago.

cover.altText: nasi minyak, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: An Indonesian rice dish typical of the Osing people of Banyuwangi, made with steamed rice, boiled vegetables, tofu, tempeh, corn fritter, and fried ariid catfish, served with kencur or terasi sambal.

cover.altText: nasi tempong, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: Indonesian steamed chicken with mushrooms and hard-boiled eggs, seasoned with soy sauce and garlic, cooked with rice in a tin bowl, and served with light chicken broth and chopped leeks.

cover.altText: nasi tim, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: Indonesian steamed rice cooked with coconut milk and spices, especially associated with Betawi and Javanese culinary traditions.

cover.altText: nasi uduk, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: Nata de coco, also called coconut gel, is a chewy, translucent, jelly-like food made by fermenting coconut water, which forms a gel through microbial cellulose produced by Komagataeibacter xylinus.

cover.altText: nata de coco: Nata de coco

list.shortDescription: A Filipino dessert of chewy, translucent, sweet-sour jelly made by fermenting pineapple juice. Produced in Pagsanjan, Laguna since the 18th century, it is used in fruit salads, jams, ice creams, and candies.
An Indonesian palm drink extracted from toddy-palm flower clusters before sunrise, sweet and translucent, and liable to ferment into toddy within hours at ambient temperature.

cover.altText: neera: 'Neera' health drink was first manufactured from Kaippuzha plant in Kollam

list.shortDescription: A Korean dish of thinly sliced beef that is marinated and grilled. Its name refers to the broad cuts of beef, and it was enjoyed at court during the Joseon period.

cover.altText: neobiani: neobiani (thinly sliced, marinated, and grilled beef)

list.shortDescription: A soup made from stinging nettles, eaten mainly in Scandinavia, Finland, Iran, Ireland, the United Kingdom, and Eastern Europe. Young nettle buds are collected in spring and early summer, and recipes vary regionally.

cover.altText: nettle soup, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: An Argentine dish of thin beef slices wrapped around a filling, secured with a toothpick and served with sauces. It is also characteristic of Chilean, Dominican Republic, Paraguayan, and Uruguayan cuisines.
A Turkish puff pastry common in the Central Black Sea Region, made from yeast dough rolled with butter, feta-style white cheese, and walnut or poppy seed, then portioned and baked.

cover.altText: nokul: Samsun'da yapılmış fındıklı ve kuru üzümlü nokul

list.shortDescription: A Cambodian breakfast noodle dish of lightly fermented rice noodles, prepared by soaking and grinding rice, drying the paste, then extruding and boiling it in water.

A Nigerian staple soup made with ground dry ogbono seeds, a major ingredient in West African cuisines with local variations across cultures. The name comes from Igbo, with other names including pekpeara, ogwi, uyo, oro, apon, goro, and goronor.

cover.altText: ogbono soup: This is an image with the theme " Health and Wellness in Africa " from:

list.shortDescription: A Nigerian cereal pudding and street food made from maize, sorghum, or millet, with grains soaked, wet-milled, sieved, strained, and boiled into pap or a creamy pudding. It may be served with moin moin, acarajé, or bread.

cover.altText: ogi: Pap served in a stainless plate

list.shortDescription: An Ainu savory soup from northern Japan, with stock flavored by fish or animal bones and kelp, without miso or soy sauce, plus meat, fish, vegetables, or wild edible plants.

cover.altText: ohaw: Ohaw, traditional Ainu soup made from vegetables, meat and stock

list.shortDescription: A traditional Korean rice-flour candy, flat and rounded, colored red with white, yellow, and green decoration. It is a staple at ancestral rites and 60th-birthday ceremonies.

cover.altText: okchundang: Okchundang is a traditional Korean sweet made of rice flour. The flat, rounded sweet is red with white, yellow, and green decoration

list.shortDescription: A Dutch beignet, a variety of doughnut traditionally eaten on New Year’s Eve, often with raisins baked inside and powdered sugar on top; one variation uses apple instead of raisins.

cover.altText: oliebol, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: An Italian appetizer of fried olives stuffed with meat, created in Ascoli Piceno in the Marche region around 1800 by private chefs using leftover meat from celebrations.

cover.altText: olive all'ascolana: « Olive all'ascolana », stuffed olives, typical recipe from the Marches – Italy

list.shortDescription: A Ghanaian staple of broken or long-grain rice cooked with extra water, beaten smooth, and shaped into large balls, usually served with groundnut or palm-nut soup.

cover.altText: omo tuo: Omo Tuo being served at a Ghanaian restaurant in Colorado

list.shortDescription: A Sundanese staple in Indonesia, oncom is a mold-fermented food with red and black varieties, closely related to tempeh.

cover.altText: oncom: oncom

list.shortDescription: Onion rings are cross-sections of onion dipped in batter or breadcrumbs and deep fried; a variant uses onion paste. Usually served as a side dish, they are also often eaten on their own.

cover.altText: onion ring: Basket of onion rings from "El Carambas" Mexican restaurant in Rochester, Minnesota

list.shortDescription: An American Chinese dish featuring fried chicken, covered in a glaze that combines sweet orange flavor with chili.

cover.altText: orange chicken, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A traditional Central Asian steamed pie among Kyrgyz, Kazakh, Uzbek, Bashkir, and Mongolian peoples, whose name refers to the rolling or wrapping used to make it.

cover.altText: oromo: Oromo dish

list.shortDescription: Japanese New Year foods associated with stacked jūbako boxes resembling bentō. The custom of eating osechi is not practiced throughout Japan; Suzu in Ishikawa is an exception.

cover.altText: osechi, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Lombard casserole of cross-cut veal shanks braised with vegetables, white wine, and broth, often finished with gremolada and served with risotto alla milanese or polenta. Its prized marrow defines the dish.

cover.altText: ossobuco, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Swedish sweet dessert traditionally made with raw milk and cheese rennet. Hälsingland and Småland versions differ in texture and grain, and it is considered an unofficial national dish of Sweden.

cover.altText: ostkaka: Ostkaka servert med is og jordbærsyltetøy

list.shortDescription: A Southeast Asian fish cake of ground fish mixed with spices, wrapped in leaf parcels, and steamed or grilled in the wrapping. It can be eaten as a snack or with steamed rice.

cover.altText: otak-otak: Otak-otak

list.shortDescription: A Portuguese pastry from Aveiro District made with egg yolks and sugar, sometimes chocolate, enclosed in small wafer capsules molded into shapes such as shells.
A Japanese rice bowl of chicken and egg, with scallions and other ingredients simmered in soy sauce and stock, served over a large bowl of rice.

cover.altText: oyakodon: A bowl of rice topped with boiled chicken and eggs

list.shortDescription: An Indonesian Minangkabau satay of cubed beef in thick yellow sauce made with rice flour, beef and offal broth, turmeric, ginger, garlic, coriander, galangal, cumin, curry powder, and salt.

cover.altText: padang satay: Sate padang Mak Sharil yang berlokasi di Jalan Sultan Agung Kota Yogyakarta

list.shortDescription: A Spanish rice dish from the Valencian Community, an identifying symbol of the region. Versions include rabbit, chicken, duck and snails; livestock; or seafood.

cover.altText: paella: Paella - original Paella from Valencia

list.shortDescription: A Karo dish from North Sumatra made from partially digested rumen grass, cooked with spices and coconut milk, cempokak and tapioca leaves, or meat in a clear soup.

cover.altText: pagit-pagit: Terites atau Pagit-Pagit khas Karo

list.shortDescription: A Nigerian palm-fruit soup with a palm cream or palm-nut base, stewed marinated meats, smoked dried fish, and aromatics, often served with starch, eba, fufu, omotuo, banku, or fonio.

cover.altText: palm nut soup: palm nut soup close up

list.shortDescription: A small Ukrainian yeast-raised bun or doughnut, made in savory or sweet versions. Its name is a diminutive of pampukh or pampukha.

cover.altText: pampushka, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Nice sandwich of pain de campagne filled with salade niçoise: raw vegetables, hard-boiled eggs, and anchovies or tuna, dressed with olive oil, salt and pepper. No mayonnaise is used; it historically used day-old bread.

cover.altText: pan-bagnat: Pan-bagnat

list.shortDescription: A flat batter bread, often thin and round, made with starch and sometimes eggs, milk, and butter, then cooked on a hot griddle or frying pan.

cover.altText: pancake: Honey poured on american pancakes. Walnuts are on top of the stack of pancakes

list.shortDescription: An Italian soup of stale bread boiled in seasoned broth or water, found across Italy in versions shaped by regional bread, liquid, and cooking methods.

cover.altText: pancotto: pane cotto con rucola

list.shortDescription: A Sardinian dish from Barbagia made with shards of pane carasau crispbread; its Sardinian name means “shredded bread.” It began as a frugal rural food and later became a staple across the island.

cover.altText: pane frattau: Pane frattau, a Sardinian dish

list.shortDescription: A Sicilian chickpea-flour fritter popular in Palermo, made with water, salt, pepper, olive oil, and finely chopped parsley. Served in bread or a sesame roll, pane e panelle sandwiches include lemon squeezed over the fritter.

cover.altText: panelle: Panelle in Caltanissetta

list.shortDescription: A chopped salad from Tuscany and Umbria, made with stale bread, onions, tomatoes, often cucumbers and sometimes basil, and dressed with olive oil and vinegar. It is popular in summer.

cover.altText: panzanella, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A snack from the Indian subcontinent made from black gram flour dough, deep-fried or cooked with dry heat until crunchy. Lentil, chickpea, rice, tapioca, millet, or potato flour may also be used.

cover.altText: papad: Bengali food

list.shortDescription: An Australian pie of parrot meat, using king parrots, crimson rosellas, or rainbow lorikeets alone or with beef and ham. Eaten into the early 20th century, it fell from general consumption after laws protected parrots.

cover.altText: parrot pie: A recipe for parrot pie from page 1259 of the 1888 edition of Mrs. Beeton's Book of Household Management

list.shortDescription: An Abruzzo cake shaped like the rough, round bread local farmers made with corn flour. Eggs mimic corn’s yellow, while dark chocolate covers it in imitation of the bread’s burnt surface. Traditionally served at Christmas.

cover.altText: parrozzo: Parrozzo, ein ital. Kuchen

list.shortDescription: A simple pasta of fresh tomatoes dressed in extra virgin olive oil and seasoned with garlic, basil, and salt, prepared as a quick, light meal rather than a heavily sauced dish.

cover.altText: pasta al pomodoro: Spaghetti al pomodoro e basilico. Autore foto: Roberto De Martino

list.shortDescription: Pasta alla gricia comes from Italy’s Lazio region and is prepared with guanciale, pecorino romano, and black pepper.

cover.altText: pasta alla gricia: Pasta alla gricia (with guanciale, pecorino romano and black pepper)

list.shortDescription: A dish of one or more kinds of pasta, called insalata di pasta or pasta fredda in Italian, usually served chilled or at room temperature and tossed in a vinegar-, oil-, or mayonnaise-based dressing.

cover.altText: pasta salad: Pasta salad close-up

list.shortDescription: A sweet tart from Italy, made principally from flour, sugar, and egg, with a thin lattice over jam or dulce de leche; it is common in Argentina, Paraguay, Uruguay, Egypt, and Greece.

cover.altText: pastafrola: Pastafrola argentina

list.shortDescription: A Portuguese crisp dough pastry filled with navy bean jam, first introduced in Torres Vedras in the early 20th century, though its earlier origins may lie with nuns.

cover.altText: pastel de feijão: L1180760

list.shortDescription: A Turkish cured meat, heavily seasoned and air-dried, typically made from water buffalo or beef and known by several names across Balkan and Mediterranean cuisines.

cover.altText: pastırma: бастурма, Basturma or Pastroma from Armenia, luftgetrockneter Schinken im Paprikamantel, Paprika leicht scharf, mit etwas Knoblauch im Paprika

list.shortDescription: A Chinese vegetable soup developed by the Teochew people during the Song dynasty’s final year, made with edible plants, mushrooms, vegetable broth, and lard. Served to the last Song emperor, it later became a way to honor him.

cover.altText: patriotic soup, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A yufka börek filled with cheese, pastirma, tomato, parsley, and pepper, all chopped into small pieces and rolled like sigara böreği but larger, then fried and served hot.

cover.altText: paçanga, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: Pea soup is made from dried peas, including split peas, and appears in many cuisines with wide regional variations. Its color ranges from greyish-green to yellow, and it has been eaten since antiquity.

cover.altText: pea soup: Finnish Pea Soup

list.shortDescription: An American sandwich of peanut butter and fruit preserves spread on bread, popularized by the accessibility of mass-produced peanut butter and long popular as an inexpensive meal and school food.

cover.altText: peanut butter and jelly sandwich: A peanut butter and jelly sandwich, made with Skippy peanut butter and Welch's grape jelly on white bread

list.shortDescription: A thrifty American sandwich of bread, peanut butter, and crunchy, tangy pickles, dating to the Depression era and noted for its appeal to stereotypical pregnancy cravings.

cover.altText: peanut butter and pickle sandwich: A cat next to a peanut butter pickle sandwich

list.shortDescription: A traditional Javanese salad with peanut sauce, commonly eaten alongside steamed rice, lontong, or ketupat.

cover.altText: pecel: Pecel, campuran sayuran dan bahan lain dengan bumbu kacang yang biasanya pedas

list.shortDescription: An ancient lamb recipe from Abruzzo’s mountain tradition, especially widespread in the Marsican area, the L’Aquila basin, and the Monti della Laga.

cover.altText: pecora alla callara: Pecora ajo cotturo

list.shortDescription: A calorie-rich North American food made from tallow, dried meat, and sometimes dried berries, eaten raw or used in stews and still prepared today.

cover.altText: pemmican: BC Bites: "Rich in Food"

list.shortDescription: A Dutch cookie-like confection tied to the early-December Sinterklaas holiday in the Netherlands and Belgium, with ingredients resembling those of German Pfeffernüsse.

cover.altText: pepernoot: Pepernoten

list.shortDescription: An Indonesian method of wrapping food in banana leaves and securing parcels with lidi seumat before steaming or charcoal-grilling them. The spice mixture presses against the main ingredients; the leaves are discarded.

cover.altText: pepes: Pais lauk mas (pepes ikan mas), a carp fish in spices and herbs cooked in banana leaf package. A popular Sundanese cuisine. The specialty cooking of Ibu Sulastri, Rawasari, Central Jakarta

list.shortDescription: Small spice cookies known in Dutch as pepernoten. They are popular holiday treats among Germans and ethnic Mennonites in North America, with similar cookies also made in Denmark.

cover.altText: pfeffernusse: One and a half pfeffernüsse commercially manufactured (in Germany), sold in Australia. With centimetre ruler for scale

list.shortDescription: Phat kaphrao is a Thai stir-fried holy basil dish that emerged as Chinese immigrants began selling it in restaurants during King Rama VII’s reign. Now a national dish, it gained popularity after 1957.

cover.altText: phat kaphrao: Basil fried crispy pork with rice (ข้าวกะเพราหมูกรอบ) as sold in Chiang Mai, Thailand

list.shortDescription: An Argentine and Uruguayan appetizer of savory snack and finger foods, related to Italian antipasto and Spanish tapas, and served as a starter or, sometimes, a main course.

cover.altText: picada, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Filipino dessert of steamed cassava flour balls mixed with sugar and lye, flavored with pandan leaves and rolled in grated coconut, cheese, or latik.

cover.altText: pichi-pichi, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Veneto dessert flan of white and yellow flour, yeast, sugar, milk, pine nuts, dried figs, raisins, fennel seeds, and grappa. Paired with red wine, it is eaten at Christmas and especially Epiphany.
A calorie- and protein-dense fish soup in Paraguay’s traditional cuisine, shaped by the food scarcity that followed the Paraguayan War of 1864–1870. In Guaraní, pira means “fish.”

cover.altText: piracaldo, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Swedish potato dumpling associated with Piteå, made mostly from raw potatoes and a blend of wheat and barley flour, in several varieties.

cover.altText: pitepalt: Pitepalt, Palt

list.shortDescription: A French round, enclosed pie made by baking two puff pastry disks around a filling. Its domed top is traditionally scored in a spiral with a knife and its edge scalloped.

cover.altText: pithivier: Un Pithiviers de faisan, restaurant Le Bologne , Genève

list.shortDescription: An Italian pizza topped with four cheeses, usually melted together, and prepared with or without tomato sauce. It is popular in Italy and worldwide.

cover.altText: pizza quattro formaggi: Italian four-cheese pizza

list.shortDescription: An Italian pizza, also called pizza 4 stagioni or la quattro stagioni, divided into four sections whose varied ingredients represent the seasons of the year.

cover.altText: pizza quattro stagioni: Pizza Quattro Stagioni

list.shortDescription: A Turkish confection of flour roasted in butter and blended into pulled sugar, shaped into fine strands and sometimes garnished with ground pistachios.

cover.altText: pişmaniye, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Louisiana sandwich traditionally filled with roast beef, ham, or fried seafood—shrimp, crawfish, fish, oysters, or crab—on a lengthwise-cut New Orleans French bread roll with a crisp crust and fluffy crumb.

cover.altText: po' boy: Shrimp Po Boy from Crabby Jack's Rastaurant in New Orleans, Louisiana. Photo Courtesy of Jason Perlow (jason@egullet.org)

list.shortDescription: A traditional Batak snack from Tapanuli, Indonesia, shaped like a clenched fist or finger and prepared either raw or steamed.
Poke consists of cubes of raw fish tossed in sauce, served either as an appetizer or a main course. In Hawaiian, the name means “to slice” or “to cut crosswise into pieces.”

cover.altText: poke, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Swedish peppermint-flavoured stick candy, white and red, invented by Amalia Eriksson in Gränna in 1859 and still sold at fairs and Christmas markets.

cover.altText: polkagris: Swedish candy "polkagrisar" for sale in Gränna, the home of the "polkagris"

list.shortDescription: A heavy, soft, crumbly Spanish shortbread made with flour, sugar, milk, and nuts, produced mostly in Andalusia and known elsewhere as mantecados.

cover.altText: polvoron: MedinaSidonia-P1060062.JPG

list.shortDescription: An American appetizer of corn kernels that expand and puff when heated, commonly eaten salted, buttered, sweetened, or with artificial flavorings.

cover.altText: popcorn: Unpopped corn kernels, prepared for popping. – Studio photo of Popcorn. Taken in 2011

list.shortDescription: Potato chips are thin potato slices deep-fried, baked, or air-fried until crunchy. They are snacks, appetizers, or sides, ranging from salted basics to varieties with herbs, spices, cheeses, flavorings, and additives.

cover.altText: potato chip: A pile of potato chips. These are Utz-brand, grandma's kettle-cooked style

list.shortDescription: A square-shaped mandu in Korean cuisine, typically served chilled in summer and dipped in soy sauce and vinegar. Gaeseong is famous for its pyeonsu.

cover.altText: pyeonsu, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: Moldavian meatballs of minced pork and beef, eggs, grated potatoes, soaked bread, onions, herbs, pepper and salt. Flattened into ovals, they are breaded and fried in hot oil; they may also be marinated in tomato sauce.

cover.altText: pârjoale: Pârjoale moldovenești (Moldauische Frikadellen)

list.shortDescription: A northern Swedish relative of Scottish haggis made with beef sinew, liver, heart, lung, onion and barley, mixed with stock, black pepper and marjoram.

cover.altText: pölsa, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: An Arabic dessert of sweet dumplings filled with cream and nuts, or folded pancakes. Batter is poured onto a hot surface and cooked on one side; the filled parcels are then fried, baked, or eaten fresh.

cover.altText: qatayef, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Mexican tortilla filled with birria-style beef and melted cheese, served with broth for dipping. Its early Tijuana version used goat meat; beef and chicken are now also used.

cover.altText: quesabirria: Quesabirria at Taqueria La Hacienda, Sonoma, California

list.shortDescription: A Mexican dish of a tortilla folded in half, or two tortillas filled with cheese and sometimes meat, spices, or other fillings, cooked on a griddle or stove.

cover.altText: quesadilla: An (opened) Squash Flower or Flor de Calabaza Empanada in Oaxaca, Mexico

list.shortDescription: An Italian meat sauce commonly served with pasta, with ragù alla bolognese as the most typical version. Other versions include napoletana, salsiccia, barese, and d’anatra.

cover.altText: ragù: Ragù fatto in casa

list.shortDescription: A Japanese-Chinese fusion noodle soup of alkaline wheat noodles in hot broth, commonly soy sauce or miso, topped with pork, nori, fermented bamboo shoots, narutomaki, and scallions.

cover.altText: ramen: 醤油ラーメン（東京ラーメン）

list.shortDescription: A Russian pirog with an opening in its top that leaves the filling exposed, a style popular in Tsarist Russia and in Moscow taverns.

cover.altText: rasstegai, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Sicilian dessert from Caltanissetta made with puff pastry and a ricotta filling, distinguished from Catania’s fried raviola by its dough composition despite a similar shape.

cover.altText: raviola di ricotta of Caltanissetta: Raviola di ricotta nissena

list.shortDescription: Ravioli are Italian stuffed pasta with a filling enclosed in thin dough, usually served in broth or with sauce. They are commonly square, though circular and semicircular forms are also used.

cover.altText: ravioli: Ravioli med skinke og asparges i mascarponecreme

list.shortDescription: A Thai curry of red paste cooked in coconut milk with meat or tofu. The paste combines dried red chilies, garlic, shallots, galangal, shrimp paste, lime leaves, lemongrass, and spices.

cover.altText: red curry: Kaeng phet mu (Thai script: แกงเผ็ดหมู): Thai red curry with pork

list.shortDescription: An American red layer cake made with baking powder, butter, buttermilk or vinegar, cocoa powder, eggs, flour, salt, vanilla extract, and usually red food coloring, finished with cream cheese or ermine icing.

cover.altText: red velvet cake: Red Velvet Cake, prepared by Waldorf Astoria New York

list.shortDescription: Mexican refried beans are cooked, mashed, then fried or baked, a staple also prepared differently in Tex-Mex cuisine and popular across Latin America.

cover.altText: refried beans, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A deep-fried savoury Indonesian-Javanese cracker made with flour and a crisp batter. Peyek kacang is the most common variety, while teri, rebon, or ebi may also be used.

cover.altText: rempeyek: Rempeyek

list.shortDescription: Indonesian thick rice crackers made from cooked glutinous rice seasoned with spices, shaped flat and rounded, sun-dried, then deep-fried in ample oil until crispy.

cover.altText: rengginang: Rengginang, Indonesian snack made of deepfried rice

list.shortDescription: A Tuscan vegetable-and-bread soup made from leftovers with cannellini beans, lacinato kale, cabbage, carrot, chard, celery, potatoes, and onion, often baked in a clay pot.

cover.altText: ribollita: Хлебная Риболлита

list.shortDescription: An Indonesian hot, spicy spice mixture from Minahasa and Gorontalo, made with chilies, shallots, garlic, ginger, coconut oil, lime leaves, lemongrass, and lime juice to season barbecued meat, seafood, or chicken.

cover.altText: rica-rica: Sambal rica (stir-fried chili sauce)

list.shortDescription: An Indonesian rice dish typical of Cirebon, Indramayu, Brebes, and Tegal, with fried tempeh and tofu, raw cucumber, boiled bean sprouts, chives, peanut sauce, light soy sauce, and fried onions.

cover.altText: rice lengko: Nasi Lengko (Sega Lengko) of Cirebon, West Java, Indonesia. Vegetarian rice with tofu and beansprout. チルボンのナシ・レンコ.ご飯の上に豆腐ともやしを載せ、ピーナッツソースとケチャップマニスをかけたもの。

list.shortDescription: A Dutch rice pie with a pudding filling, native to Verviers and popular around Eastern Belgium, southeastern Netherlands, and Aachen. Traditionally made with unpasteurized cow’s milk.

cover.altText: rijstevlaai, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A French haute-cuisine dessert made by setting rice pudding with Bavarian cream in a charlotte mold, unmolding it, and decorating it with candied fruits steeped in alcohol such as kirsch or maraschino.

cover.altText: riz à l'impératrice: extrait du livre de Gustave Garlin La pâtissier moderne 1889

list.shortDescription: Roast beef is roasted beef, generally served as a main course. In the Anglosphere, it is often eaten at Sunday lunch or dinner with Yorkshire pudding; sliced or leftover beef can also be used in cold cuts, sandwiches, or hash.

cover.altText: roast beef: Rostas, ready and served

list.shortDescription: Japanese robatayaki, or robata, is a barbecue-like method for grilling food at varying speeds over hot charcoal on a wide, flat open fireplace in the irori style. It traditionally features morsels of seafood and vegetables.

cover.altText: robatayaki: Robatayaki restaurant, Osaka

list.shortDescription: A Javanese salad commonly found in Indonesia, Malaysia, and Singapore, made with sliced fruit and vegetables and served with a spicy palm sugar dressing.

cover.altText: rojak: Rujak Buah is an Indonesian Fruit Salad. It is made of a mixture of fruits and spicy peanut sauce. Pestle and mortar sets are commonly used to make the sauce and to toss the mixture

list.shortDescription: One of Cuba’s national dishes, made with stewed beef and tomatoes in a sofrito base. Its name may refer to leftovers from other meals or the meat’s tattered appearance.

cover.altText: ropa vieja: Ropa Vieja, a traditional Cuban dish

list.shortDescription: A popular eastern Indian and South Asian dessert of ball-shaped chhena-dough dumplings cooked in light sugar syrup until the syrup permeates them.

cover.altText: rosogolla: 'Rasgulla'. This is a famous sweet-dish, of Bengal origin but is enjoyed in the whole country. It is made up of cottage cheese and soaked in sugar syrup

list.shortDescription: An Indonesian baked bread pastry with croissant-like crust layers, made from flour laminated with butter or margarine and filled with cheese and banana. Other variants feature durian, reflecting European pastry influences.

cover.altText: roti bolen: Durian Keju Bollen, Kartika Sari brand pastry filled with cheese and durian cream. Specialty of Bandung, West Java, Indonesia

list.shortDescription: An Indonesian rectangular brown bread made with sesame seeds, cinnamon, and palm sugar. Known as roti ganjel rel in Javanese cuisine, it is associated with Betawi people in Jakarta.

cover.altText: roti gambang: Cinnamon and palm sugar bread

list.shortDescription: A Creole spiced tomato sauce common in Mauritius, Réunion, the Seychelles, and other Francophone Indian Ocean and West Indies areas, combining French, Asian, and East African culinary traits.

cover.altText: rougail: Photo personnelle de David Remi (davremi@yahoo.fr), Assiette de rougail saucisse

list.shortDescription: A Chinese dried meat product with a light, fluffy texture like coarse cotton, golden in color, and a distinctive sweet flavor comparable to beef jerky.

cover.altText: rousong: Fragrance Brand Pork Floss taken by Eddie Khoo in February 2006

list.shortDescription: A Javanese Osing salad from Banyuwangi, East Java, combining beef soto and rujak cingur. Rujak vegetables and lontong rice cake are served with petis sauce and soto soup, alongside es temulawak made from Curcuma zanthorrhiza.
An Arab dish of lentils made with pomegranate juice, with roots reaching back to at least the 10th century.
A graham-cracker sandwich filled with chocolate and toasted marshmallow, typically prepared over a campfire so the heat melts the chocolate; popular in the United States and Canada.

cover.altText: s'more: A S'mores made with a half a Hershey's chocolate bar, Nabisco graham crackers and a marshmallow that has been melted in the microwave

list.shortDescription: A saffron pancake from Gotland, Sweden, made by baking rice pudding, cream, milk, sugar, egg, chopped almonds, and saffron together. Served tepid or cold with dewberry jam and whipped cream.

cover.altText: saffron pancake: Saffranspannkaka med salmbär (blåhallon) och vispad grädde

list.shortDescription: A Syracuse, New York, dish of young potatoes served in summer and common at fairs and barbecues across Central New York. Potatoes intended for it are sold by the bag with packages of salt.

cover.altText: salt potatoes: Cooking salt potatoes in Syracuse, July 2005

list.shortDescription: A Bolivian baked empanada with hard, sweet pastry, filled with beef, pork, or chicken in a sweet, slightly spicy sauce containing ají, potatoes, and sometimes egg.

cover.altText: salteña: Salteñas, a Bolivian empanada filled with beef or chicken, mixed in a sweet, lightly spicy sauce and containing chopped potatoes, raisins and hard eggs

list.shortDescription: A liquorice confection flavored with salmiak salt, also called salmiak liquorice, salmiac liquorice, or salmiakki, common in Nordic countries, Benelux, and northern Germany.

cover.altText: salty licorice: Swedish salty liquorice "Djungelvrål" (in English: roar of the jungle)

list.shortDescription: An Indonesian hot and spicy shrimp dish, with shrimp peeled or left unpeeled and stir-fried in sambal paste with a little cooking oil.

cover.altText: sambal shrimp: Sambal goreng udang

list.shortDescription: A Cambodian soup and staple food in Cambodia's villages, made with chicken or fish stock, lemongrass or green kroeung, vegetables, mushrooms, freshwater fish, coconut blossom, fish sauce, rice powder, and fresh herbs.

cover.altText: samlor prahal: Sam Khmer Noodles (Num Banhchok Samlar Brahar), Siem Reap, Cambodia

list.shortDescription: A blood dish from rural Occitania, made by immediately collecting and cooking fresh livestock blood, usually as a crêpe or pancake that varies by town, including Spanish Occitania.

cover.altText: sanganhèta: Extrait de Nancy artiste du dimanche 16 mai 1886, fascicule n° 18, p. 158

list.shortDescription: A Peruvian dish of chicken blood seasoned with garlic, onion, chili pepper, and herbs, and prepared with baked potatoes, fried sweet potatoes, or cassava.

cover.altText: sangrecita: Desayuno típico de Perú

list.shortDescription: A Filipino layered dessert of glutinous rice and coconut, made with rice flour, coconut milk, sugar, water, flavoring, and coloring. Each layer is colored separately and usually topped with latik or grated coconut.

cover.altText: sapin-sapin: Sapin-sapin is one of delicacy well known in the Philippines

list.shortDescription: An Ottoman dish of grape, vine, or cabbage leaves rolled around minced meat, rice, or both. Called sarma in Turkish, the name also appears in Armenian and several Central and Eastern European languages.

cover.altText: sarma: Yaprak sarma, Kayseri style, at a Kayseri restaurant in Ankara

list.shortDescription: Stuffed grape, vine, or cabbage leaves wrapped around minced meat, rice, or both. Known in Turkish as sarma, the dish is widespread across Europe, the Middle East, and South Asia.

cover.altText: sarmale: Yaprak sarma, Kayseri style, at a Kayseri restaurant in Ankara

list.shortDescription: Indonesian satay made by grilling goat meat mixed with seasoning, also known as mutton satay, lamb satay, or goat satay.

cover.altText: sate kambing: Mutton satay from H. Faqih, Jombang, 2017-09-19

list.shortDescription: A Finnish meat dish of thinly sliced reindeer steak or back, fried in fat with salt and black pepper, then cooked with water, cream, or beer until tender. In Finland, it is often served with pickled cucumber.

cover.altText: sautéed reindeer: Sautéed reindeer with mashed potatoes, lingonberry and gherkin. Photo taken with Nokia 6230i in a restaurant (Hotel Jeris, Muonio, Finland. Thanks!)

list.shortDescription: An Indonesian vegetable soup from Sundanese cuisine, with peanuts, young jackfruit, young melinjo leaves and unpeeled seeds, bilimbi, chayote, long beans, and often corn cooked in tamarind broth, sometimes with beef stock.

cover.altText: sayur asem: Sayur asem, Indonesian vegetable soup. 「サユ－ル・アッスム」インドネシアの野菜スープ

list.shortDescription: A Middle European bread dumpling made from dried wheat rolls, milk, and eggs, usually served as a side dish but sometimes as a main course or dessert.

cover.altText: serviettenknödel: Serviettenkloß, nach Thüringer Familienrezept selbst hergestellt Hauptzutaten: Wasser, Milch, Semmeln, Eier, Muskatnuss, Salz, In Serviette ca. 40 Minuten gekocht

list.shortDescription: An American layered salad of iceberg lettuce, tomatoes, cucumbers, onions, sweet peas, hard-boiled eggs, sharp cheddar cheese, and bacon, topped with mayonnaise dressing and sometimes sour cream.

cover.altText: seven-layer salad, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Maghrebi dish of eggs poached in tomatoes, olive oil, peppers, onion, and garlic, flavored with cumin, paprika, and cayenne pepper. Popular across North Africa and the Middle East.

cover.altText: shakshuka: Shakshuka

list.shortDescription: A Japanese kakigōri dessert of shaved ice flavored with condensed milk and accompanied by small colorful mochi, fruit, and sweet bean paste, usually azuki bean paste.

cover.altText: shirokuma, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: An Iranian rice pudding of saffron, sugar, rose water, butter, cinnamon, and cardamom. Often made in large quantities for religious ceremonies, it is especially used to break the fast during Ramadan.

cover.altText: sholezard: Sholezard, an Iranian traditional dessert

list.shortDescription: A Sichuan Chinese dish of meat poached with water, starch, and salt, layered over boiled vegetables with garlic, dried chili, and Sichuan pepper, then finished with smoking-hot vegetable oil.

cover.altText: shuizhu: ​简体中文：水煮牛肉 繁體中文：水煮牛肉

list.shortDescription: A Scottish dish of oatmeal fried with onions and seasonings in suet, lard, beef dripping, or butter. Its name comes from the frying sound; it is served with potatoes or mince and tatties, especially in northeast Scotland.

A thick Greek potato purée made with garlic, walnuts, almonds, or liquid-soaked stale bread, olive oil, and vinegar, usually prepared in a mortar and pestle. Served with batter-fried cod, especially during Lent and on March 25.

cover.altText: skordalia, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A hamburger-bun sandwich filled with seasoned ground meat, typically beef, onions, tomato sauce or ketchup, Worcestershire sauce, and other seasonings.

cover.altText: sloppy joe, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Chinese confection from Hong Kong with a glutinous rice skin, eaten cold during the Mid-Autumn Festival. Usually made and sold by bakeries, it is not baked in ovens like traditional cakes.

cover.altText: snow skin mooncake: the-cooking-of-joy.blogspot.com/2019/08/snowskin-cake-tru

list.shortDescription: An Ugandan cassava-leaf stew of freshly mashed leaves combined with fish, groundnut paste, or meat such as beef, goat, or pork. It is served mainly with bundu, and also with rice, posho, matooke, or Ggonja.

cover.altText: sombe, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Polish and Eastern European soup made with water or broth, sorrel leaves, and salt; versions add or substitute spinach, chard, nettle, garden orache, dandelion, goutweed, or ramsons.

cover.altText: sorrel soup: Sorrel soup with egg and croutons

list.shortDescription: A Haitian beef soup based on squash, known as pumpkin soup in French and squash or pumpkin in Creole. It was added to UNESCO’s Intangible Cultural Heritage List in 2021.

cover.altText: soup joumou: Chaudron de soupe de giraumon, un plat traditionnel haïtien

list.shortDescription: A Polish traditional soup whose fermented rye, wheat, and oats form a sourdough-like base, stirred into stock that may include boiled sausage, bacon, hard-boiled eggs, potatoes, and dried mushrooms.

An Italian pasta dish from the coastal regions, especially southern Italy: spaghetti cooked with fresh clams, garlic, parsley, and olive oil, sometimes white wine. It has numerous regional variations.

cover.altText: spaghetti alle vongole: Spaghetti with clams (Alassio, Italy)

list.shortDescription: An Italian-American pasta of spaghetti, tomato, and meatballs, developed by Italian immigrants in New York City with inspiration from southern Italy and now regarded as a classic across the United States.

cover.altText: spaghetti with meatballs: Spaghetti and meatballs

list.shortDescription: A savory spinach pie of Greek origin, filled with chopped spinach, egg, and usually feta or white cheese. It is eaten throughout Greece, Bosnia and Herzegovina, and Turkey.

cover.altText: spanakopita: Spanakopita

list.shortDescription: Swabian egg pasta with an irregular, rough, porous shape, pressed or dripped through a perforated plate into boiling water or steam. Usually a side for meat with sauce, or a main with cheese and onion.

cover.altText: spätzle: Spätzle, hergestellt mit Spätzlehobel

list.shortDescription: A French dish of raw minced beef, seasoned with onions, capers, parsley or chives, salt, pepper, and Worcestershire sauce, and commonly topped with a raw egg yolk.

cover.altText: steak tartare: Sydney Food Blog Review of Le Grande Bouffe, Rozelle: Classic Steak Tartare

list.shortDescription: A Flemish dish of mashed or puréed potatoes and root vegetables, found in Belgium, northern France and the Netherlands, with optional cream, bacon, onion or shallot, herbs and spices.

cover.altText: stoemp: Cod and stoemp

list.shortDescription: An Italian soup of meat broth with small shreds of egg mixture, prepared by drizzling the mixture into boiling broth and stirring. It is popular around Rome in Lazio.

cover.altText: stracciatella, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: Strapačky are dumplings popular in Slovakia and Hungary. The Slovak version pairs halušky with stewed sauerkraut rather than bryndza; the Hungarian version traditionally includes juhtúró, a local equivalent of bryndza.

cover.altText: strapačky: Strapačky

list.shortDescription: A Polish pasta dish with cooked pasta covered in strawberry and cream sauce, eaten at lunch or as dessert and often served in schools.

cover.altText: strawberry pasta: Strawberry Pasta

list.shortDescription: A northern Russian and Siberian Arctic dish of raw, thin, long-sliced frozen freshwater whitefish salmonids, including nelma, muksun, chir, and omul. Around Lake Baikal, it is called raskolotka.

cover.altText: stroganina: Блюдо строганина на столе

list.shortDescription: A Bosnian specialty of Mostar, these Turkish-named stuffed onions pack minced beef and rice into onion leaves, simmer them in broth, and serve them with dense natural yogurt.

cover.altText: stuffed onions: Gatim tradicional Kosovarëi njohur si speca dollma nga turqishtja

list.shortDescription: A squash or zucchini dolma common in Egypt, the Levant and the Balkans, stuffed with rice and sometimes meat, then cooked on the stovetop or in the oven. The meat version is served hot as a main course.
A Lao and Northeastern Thai dish of spice-flavored beef brisket, grilled rare, sliced, and served with sticky rice and other dishes. Its name means “crying tiger.”

cover.altText: suea rong hai: Suea rong hai (Thai script: เสือร้องไห้) literally means "weeping tiger". It is grilled marinated beef which is eaten with vegetables and Nam chim chaeo dipping sauce

list.shortDescription: A northern Italian dessert combining red grape must with flour and sugar. It is slowly cooked and cooled, then served like pudding or preserved in jars like jam.

cover.altText: sugolo: sûg 'd ùa

list.shortDescription: A Korean soup of hand-torn dough flakes with various vegetables, similar in flavor and recipe to noodle-based kalguksu. It is commonly eaten on rainy days with bindaetteok.

cover.altText: sujebi: sujebi (hand-torn noodle soup)

list.shortDescription: A Turkish dry, spicy, fermented sausage made from minced meat and animal fat, generally beef or lamb; beef predominates in Turkey.

cover.altText: sujuk: Turkish sujuk (industrially produced), made of beef, minced with garlic, cumin and other spices

list.shortDescription: A Turkish stew or thick soup with köfte: meatballs of minced beef, rice or bulgur, onion, and spices, boiled in gravy with tomato sauce, olive oil, and Turkish red pepper paste.

cover.altText: sulu köfte: Plate with Turkish food: "Sulu köfte"

list.shortDescription: A lightly salted, fermented Baltic Sea herring in northern Swedish cuisine since at least the 16th century. It ferments in weak brine for at least six months, developing a strong smell and somewhat acidic taste.

cover.altText: surströmming: Surströmming – a fish speciality from north Sweden

list.shortDescription: An American Japanese-Mexican fusion roll prepared by wrapping fish and vegetables and serving it like a burrito, though it is not considered authentic to either cuisine.

cover.altText: sushi burrito: View on Instagram www.instagram.com/p/BqBZ81pHknc/

list.shortDescription: A Canadian fusion of sushi and pizza from Toronto, built on a slightly crisp, chewy fried rice patty, topped with avocado, salmon, tuna or crab, blended mayonnaise and wasabi powder, and cut into wedges.

cover.altText: sushi pizza: Sushi pizza

list.shortDescription: A Peruvian dessert dating to mid-19th-century Lima, made with manjar blanco—a milk-based confection—and meringue, and now common in coastal cities and Peruvian restaurants abroad.

cover.altText: suspiro de limeña: "Suspiro limeño" is a traditional dessert of Peruvian cuisine having its origin in the Peruvian capital (Lima). It is also known as "Supiro de limeña" or even as "Suspiro a la limeña"

list.shortDescription: A Nigerian Hausa dish of thin-sliced, spiced meat smoke-grilled on wooden skewers, made with beef, lamb, goat, ram, chicken, kidney, liver, tripe, or shrimp; it is popular as an evening street snack or appetizer.

cover.altText: suya, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Chinese Indonesian frog-leg dish seasoned with garlic, ginger, fermented soy paste, salt, and pepper. It may be served as soup, deep-fried, or stir-fried, usually with plain white steamed rice.

cover.altText: swikee: Kodok Oh is a kind of Swikee, Chinese Indonesian frog leg dish, cooked in tauco (fermented soybean paste) soup. Jalan Gajah Mada, Jakarta, Indonesia

list.shortDescription: A Vietnamese pork chop marinated with lemongrass and fish sauce, glazed with liquid caramel, and charcoal-grilled.

cover.altText: sườn nướng, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Scottish confection made by boiling sugar, condensed milk, and butter to a soft-ball stage, then allowing it to crystallise. Vanilla is a common flavour, and nut pieces are sometimes added.

cover.altText: tablet: A photograph of Butter Tablet

list.shortDescription: Taboon bread is baked on hot stones inside a portable clay tabun oven, a truncated cone with a top opening and sometimes a bottom opening for stoking the fire; these ovens are common in Jordan and Palestine.

cover.altText: taboon bread: Tabun oven set against backdrop showing a straw-woven plate and dough-kneading bowl (from the Museum of the Palestine Institute, Jerusalem)

list.shortDescription: Tagine malsouka is a Tunisian dish of layered malsouka dough, made by sticking raw dough to a heated pan, then filling it with eggs, vegetables, or meat. It is often enjoyed cold as finger food.

cover.altText: tagine malsouka: Tajine malsouka originaire de Tunisie

list.shortDescription: An East Javanese mixed-tofu dish of fried tofu, lontong, lentho or perkedel, bean sprouts, lettuce, yellow noodles, and krupuk in spiced beef stew with petis shrimp paste, topped with fried onions and sambal chili sauce.

cover.altText: tahu campur, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A savory Sundanese deep-fried tofu from Sumedang, West Java, with a light-brown mottled shell and a creamier, partly or wholly hollow center, served with lontong, sambal, soy sauce, or cabe rawit.

cover.altText: tahu sumedang: Sumedang tofu, snack from Sumedang, West Java, Indonesia

list.shortDescription: A grilled chicken satay served without peanut or kecap seasoning, with salt, key lime, and chili as its only seasonings. Sambal and squeezed key lime accompany it, and it is sold at night.

cover.altText: taichan satay: Contoh Sate Taichan yang dijual di daerah Senayan, Jakarta

list.shortDescription: A Maghrebi stew named for its two-part clay pot, whose conical cover returns condensation so spiced meat, poultry, or fish braises with vegetables or fruit in minimal water.

cover.altText: tajine: الطاجين المغربي من الاكلات الشعبية بالمغرب وفيه أنواع طاجين الخضر و طاجين الدجاج و طاجين اللحم و طاجين السمك

list.shortDescription: A traditional Mesoamerican dish of masa, a dough made from nixtamalized corn, steamed in a corn husk or banana leaves and filled with meats, cheeses, fruits, vegetables, herbs, chilies, or other preparations according to taste.

cover.altText: tamale: Tamal oaxaqueño de pollo, alimento tradicional mexicano

list.shortDescription: A Southwestern U.S. casserole built like a pie: a dish lined with tamale dough, filled with spiced meats, stews, or leftovers and sometimes beans, salsa, or tomatoes, then topped with dough and baked, sometimes with cheese.

cover.altText: tamale pie: A whole tamale pie

list.shortDescription: A Mexican dish of small rolled corn tortillas filled with beef, cheese, or chicken, then shallow- or deep-fried and topped with condiments such as sour cream or guacamole. Larger versions are known as flautas.

cover.altText: taquito: Burros & Fries Clairemont Mesa

list.shortDescription: A small pastry basket baked in a special mold, usually with shortcrust pastry and intended to be filled afterward. European fillings include fruit with custard or cream, flan, or chocolate.

cover.altText: tartlet: Жюльен с копченой курицей. Шампиньоны, лук. Запечен под сыром в тарталетках. Фото перед помещением в духовку

list.shortDescription: A Turkish milk pudding made from boiled white chicken breast, shredded or pounded smooth, then mixed with milk, sugar, cracked rice, thickeners, and often cinnamon. It was served to Ottoman sultans at Topkapı Palace.

cover.altText: tavukgöğsü: A sweet, gelatinous, milk pudding dessert quite similar to kazandibi, to which very thinly peeled chicken breast is added to give a chewy texture

list.shortDescription: An Italian-American pasta dish of diced poultry or seafood in a butter, cream, or milk-and-cheese sauce flavored with sherry or white wine, served with linguine, spaghetti, or egg noodles.

cover.altText: tetrazzini, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Moroccan sweet sauce of caramelized onions, raisins, cinnamon, and honey, often served on couscous.

cover.altText: tfaya: Aerial view of a plate of Moroccan couscous with Tfaya and Moroccan roasted chicken, made by Moroccan Leila Khairawi

list.shortDescription: An Acehnese steamed banana dumpling made with glutinous rice flour, ground banana, and coconut milk, filled with sweetened serikaya or grated coconut mixed with sugar, and wrapped in banana leaves.

cover.altText: timphan: Acehnese snack, timphan

list.shortDescription: A porridge specialty of Manado cuisine, also called bubur manado or Manadonese porridge, popular for breakfast in Manado and North Sulawesi, Indonesia.

cover.altText: tinutuan porridge: Tinutuan (vegetable rice porridge)

list.shortDescription: A Greek spread of feta, sometimes combined with soft white cheeses, hot and roasted peppers, olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, yogurt, and oregano. It is eaten with warm pita or as part of a mezze platter.

cover.altText: tirokafteri, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A Thai soup of shrimp in a spicy, sour broth, often served with steamed rice and sometimes with chili paste and lime juice. It may have a creamy, mellow broth or a clear, strongly flavored one.

cover.altText: tom yum kung, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: An Indonesian stew of goat meat, mutton, or beef in curry-like soup with vegetables and kecap manis, common in Central Java from Surakarta to Yogyakarta and believed to have begun in Klego, Boyolali.

cover.altText: tongseng: Tongseng, a Javanese spicy and rather sweet goat meat soup. Specialty of Solo (Surakarta), Central Java, Indonesia

list.shortDescription: An Italian layer cake from Ivrea, torta 900 combines chocolate sponge cake with a filling of mascarpone, whipped cream, and chocolate.

cover.altText: torta 900: Fetta di Torta 900 della Pasticceria Balla

list.shortDescription: A Mexican and Guatemalan dish based on a flat or bowl-shaped corn tortilla that is deep-fried or toasted. It may be eaten alone or serve as a base for other foods.

cover.altText: tostada: Contramar, Roma Norte, CDMX, Mexico

list.shortDescription: A Swiss cake from the Canton of Jura made with leavened dough and topped with a sour cream-based mix, especially popular around local festivities such as St. Martin’s Day.

cover.altText: totché: Totché is a traditional sour cream-based cake of the Canton of Jura

list.canonicalName: tripes à la mode de Caen
list.shortDescription: A traditional Normandy dish of cut-up beef stomach, large intestine, hooves, and bones, cooked with cider and calvados in a dough-sealed earthenware pot for fifteen hours.

cover.altText: tripes à la mode de Caen, a photograph of the dish

list.shortDescription: A sweet Turkish holiday bread made with flour, milk, butter, eggs, and sugar, flavored with lemon or orange zest, mastic resin, or mahleb.

cover.altText: tsoureki: Christmas 2011

list.shortDescription: A Korean dish of small garae-tteok rice cakes seasoned with spicy gochujang, often paired with eomuk, boiled eggs, and scallions. A less common soy-sauce version is called gungjung-tteokbokki.

cover.altText: tteokbokki: Korean Tteokbokki (rice cakes in sauce)

list.shortDescription: An Egyptian deep-fried confection made from unleavened choux pastry dough, piped into strips about 3 inches long, fried until golden, and soaked in sweet syrup while still hot.

cover.altText: tulumba: Picture of tulumba taken in Macedonia

list.shortDescription: An Indonesian cone-shaped rice dish from Javanese cuisine, served with vegetable and meat sides for the slametan ceremony. Cooked in a woven bamboo cone, the rice may be plain steamed, uduk, or yellow.

cover.altText: tumpeng: This is a picture of a Javanese yellow rice 'cake'. Made by and courtesy of Taufik Thoyib and Joyce from the toko Oostersch Huisje , The Hague, Holland

map.shortDescription: A layered casserole of fried eggplant, spiced minced meat, and béchamel sauce, baked until golden. Considered the national dish of Greece.
An Indonesian fried rice dish cooked with kecap manis (sweet soy sauce), shallots, garlic, tamarind, and chilli, typically topped with a fried egg.
A dish of roasted marinated chicken chunks (chicken tikka) in a spiced, creamy tomato sauce. Often considered a British national dish due to its invention in Glasgow.
A mixed rice dish of layered basmati rice, marinated meat (typically chicken, mutton, or goat), fried onions, saffron, and whole spices. The Hyderabadi version is among the most famous.
A Québécois dish of french fries topped with cheese curds and hot gravy. Originated in rural Quebec in the 1950s.
A Roman pasta made with just Pecorino Romano cheese and freshly ground black pepper tossed with hot pasta water and tonnarelli or spaghetti.
Deep-fried balls or patties of ground chickpeas, fava beans, or both, mixed with herbs and spices. A staple of Middle Eastern street food.
A Neapolitan pizza topped with San Marzano tomato sauce, fresh mozzarella, fresh basil, and olive oil. Named for Queen Margherita of Savoy in 1889.
A traditional Japanese dish of vinegared rice paired with various ingredients, most commonly raw seafood, vegetables, and sometimes tropical fruits.
A thin, breaded, pan-fried veal cutlet, traditionally served in Austria with a slice of lemon and either potato salad or parsley potatoes.
A Brazilian stew of black beans with pork and beef, served with rice, collard greens, farofa (toasted cassava flour), and orange slices.
A Hungarian soup or stew of meat and vegetables seasoned with paprika and other spices. The name derives from the Hungarian word gulyás, meaning 'herdsman'.
A Korean rice dish of steamed white rice topped with sautéed and seasoned vegetables, beef, a raw or fried egg, and gochujang (chilli paste).
A French beef stew braised in red wine (traditionally Burgundy) with beef broth, bacon, onions, mushrooms, and a bouquet garni.
A Peruvian dish of raw fish cured in fresh citrus juices (typically lime), spiced with ají or chili peppers, and seasoned with onions, salt, and cilantro.
A sandwich consisting of a cooked ground-meat patty (usually beef) between two pieces of bread or a bun. The modern form is most associated with the United States.
A West African one-pot rice dish of long-grain rice simmered in a tomato-and-red-pepper sauce with onions, garlic, ginger, thyme, and assorted proteins.
A Vietnamese sandwich of a short baguette with grilled pork, pâté, pickled vegetables, fresh herbs, and chili. A legacy of French colonial rule.
A cold Andalusian soup made from raw blended vegetables — typically tomato, cucumber, pepper, garlic, olive oil, vinegar, and stale bread.
A dish of poached chicken served with seasoned rice cooked in chicken broth, accompanied by cucumber, chili sauce, and ginger paste.
Filled dumplings of unleavened dough, traditionally stuffed with potato, sauerkraut, meat, cheese, or fruit. A staple of Polish cuisine.
A slow-cooked North African stew named after the conical clay pot in which it is cooked. Combines meat (typically lamb or chicken) with vegetables, fruits, and warming spices.
A Levantine dip or spread made from cooked, mashed chickpeas blended with tahini, lemon juice, garlic, and olive oil.
A Korean stew made with aged kimchi, pork or tuna, tofu, scallions, and gochujang, simmered together until bubbling and tangy.
A Vietnamese noodle soup of bone broth, rice noodles, herbs, and meat (typically beef or chicken). Considered Vietnam's national dish.
A stir-fried rice noodle dish from Thailand with eggs, vegetables, tofu or shrimp, peanuts, and a tangy sauce of tamarind, fish sauce, and palm sugar.
A Valencian rice dish with saffron, olive oil, vegetables, and a choice of seafood, meat, or beans. Cooked in a wide, shallow pan over an open fire.
A Japanese noodle soup with wheat noodles in a meat- or fish-based broth, flavoured with soy sauce or miso and topped with ingredients like sliced pork, nori, and scallions.
A Middle Eastern dish of slow-roasted, thinly sliced meat (lamb, mutton, beef, chicken, or mixed) served in a flatbread with vegetables and tahini or yogurt sauce.
An upside-down French tart in which apples are caramelised in butter and sugar beneath a pastry crust, then flipped when served.
A hot and sour Thai soup with shrimp, lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, galangal, lime juice, fish sauce, and crushed chili peppers.
Indonesian meatballs made from beef, chicken, or fish, served in a clear noodle soup with greens, tofu, fried shallots, and chili sauce.

A West Sumatran dry curry of beef slow-cooked for hours in coconut milk and a paste of ginger, galangal, turmeric, chili, lemongrass, garlic, and shallots until the sauce fully reduces and the meat darkens.
Twice-fried green-plantain slices, flattened between fryings. A staple across the Caribbean and Latin American coastlines, served as a side or snack, often with garlic mojo or a saltfish topping.
A Bahian (Brazilian) street food of black-eyed pea fritters split open and stuffed with vatapá (a shrimp and peanut paste), dried shrimp, and a bright salad of tomato, onion, and cilantro.
Palembang fish cakes made from ground mackerel or other white fish mixed with tapioca flour, formed into logs or balls, boiled, sliced, and fried, served with a sweet-sour-spicy cuko sauce.
A Portuguese dish of shredded salt cod stir-fried with onions, matchstick potatoes, parsley, olives, and eggs, finished with black olives and a squeeze of lemon.

A Balinese minced-meat satay: finely ground pork, chicken, or fish mixed with grated coconut, coconut milk, lime leaves, lemongrass, and spices, molded around bamboo skewers and grilled over coconut charcoal.

A Goan curry of Portuguese origin: meat (traditionally pork) marinated in vinegar, garlic, and Kashmiri chili, then cooked with onions, ginger, and warm spices. The Portuguese carne de vinha d'alhos became vindaloo over centuries.

A sour soup of Eastern European origin built on beetroots, which give it a deep red color, combined with cabbage, potatoes, carrots, onion, and a meat broth. Often served with sour cream and pampushky.
An Indonesian salad of blanched and steamed vegetables, hard-boiled egg, fried tofu, and lontong, dressed in a peanut sauce sweetened with palm sugar and spiked with chili and tamarind.
Mexican tacos of marinated pork cooked on a vertical spit, shaved onto small corn tortillas, and finished with onion, cilantro, salsa, and pineapple.
Tiny steamed semolina grains of Maghrebi origin, served beneath or alongside a stew of meat (typically lamb or chicken) and vegetables flavored with ras el hanout, saffron, and preserved lemon.

A thin, crispy South Indian crepe made from a fermented batter of rice and urad dal, served with coconut chutney and sambar. Sambar is closely related to the rasam and other lentil-stew traditions of the Deccan.
A baked or fried pastry turnover filled with seasoned meat, cheese, or vegetables. Found across Latin America from Argentina to the Philippines, each region claiming its own folded style and filling.
A Northern Thai coconut-curry noodle soup of soft egg noodles in a turmeric-and-chili coconut broth, topped with crispy fried noodles, chicken or beef, pickled mustard greens, shallots, and lime.
The national dish of Jordan: lamb cooked in a fermented dried-yogurt sauce (jameed) and served over a flatbread (shrak) topped with rice and almonds. Central to Bedouin hospitality.

A Himalayan steamed dumpling of Tibetan origin, made from a thin wheat-flour wrapper and a filling of ground meat or vegetables. Now widely eaten across Nepal, Sikkim, Bhutan, and the Tibetan diaspora.
A Balinese whole-roasted suckling pig stuffed with a spice paste of turmeric, coriander, galangal, garlic, and chili, spit-roasted over coconut husk fire until the skin crackles.

A Balinese rice plate featuring a small mound of white rice surrounded by several small portions: a meat or fish, vegetables, peanut sauce, fried shallots, shredded coconut, sambal, and a small portion of lawar.
A South Asian savory fritter made from a ground legume or grain batter, shaped into rings or patties and fried until crisp outside and tender within.

A long-simmered rice porridge eaten across East and Southeast Asia, served plain or with pickles, century egg, shredded pork, fish, or scallions. Cantonese jook, Japanese okayu, and Indonesian bubur are all forms.
A Korean stir-fried glass-noodle dish made from sweet-potato starch noodles tossed with beef, spinach, mushrooms, carrots, and onion in a sesame-oil and soy sauce dressing.

Northern Chinese crescent-shaped dumplings with a thin wheat-flour wrapper and a filling of ground pork, cabbage, ginger, scallions, and soy sauce. Boiled (shuijiao), steamed (zhengjiao), or pan-fried (guotie).

A spicy noodle soup of Peranakan and broader Southeast Asian origin: rice vermicelli or thick wheat noodles in a fragrant broth built from lemongrass, galangal, candlenuts, turmeric, and dried shrimp, topped with bean sprouts, prawns, and hard-boiled egg.
A Sichuan dish of silken tofu simmered in a fiery red sauce of fermented broad-bean paste (doubanjiang), ground pork or beef, douchi, Sichuan peppercorns, chili oil, and scallions.
An East Javanese beef soup with a deep black color from keluak nuts, seasoned with garlic, shallots, ginger, turmeric, and aromatic leaves.
A Northern Italian short-grain rice dish cooked in a bone-marrow-enriched beef broth with saffron and onions, giving it a deep yellow color and a faintly metallic, floral finish.
Eggs poached in a spiced sauce of tomatoes, peppers, onions, garlic, and chili. Origin disputed between North African and Levantine kitchens; eaten across Israel, Tunisia, Libya, and the Maghreb.
An Indonesian clear chicken soup fragrant with turmeric, lemongrass, and lime leaves, served with rice or vermicelli, shredded chicken, boiled egg, bean sprouts, and crispy shallots.

Masa (nixtamalized corn dough) filled with meat, cheese, beans, or chilies, wrapped in a corn husk or banana leaf and steamed. Found across Mexico, Guatemala, and much of Central America; deeply rooted in Mesoamerican cooking.

A layered Italian dessert of espresso-soaked savoiardi biscuits and a mascarpone cream, dusted with cocoa. Origins contested between Veneto and Friuli-Venezia Giulia; emerged in its modern form in the 1960s–80s.

Thick Japanese wheat noodles served in a light dashi-based broth, often with toppings such as tempura, sliced scallion, or a soft-boiled egg. Related to ramen but chewier and usually served in a milder broth.
A dry Indian curry of potatoes and cauliflower cooked with turmeric, cumin, ginger, garlic, and other regional spices.
A crisp, triangular pastry filled with spiced potatoes, peas, lentils, meat, or vegetables and fried or baked across South Asia and its diaspora.
Soft, steamed South Indian cakes made from a fermented batter of rice and black gram, traditionally served with sambar and coconut or tomato chutney.
Roasted marinated chicken simmered in a smooth tomato, butter, and cream sauce seasoned with fenugreek and warm spices.
A North Indian combination of spiced chickpea curry and bhature, a large, leavened, deep-fried bread served hot with pickles, onion, and chutney.
A thin, crisp South Indian fermented rice-and-lentil crepe filled with a fragrant potato masala and served with sambar and chutney.
Cubes of fresh paneer cheese served in a smooth spinach sauce seasoned with ginger, garlic, green chili, and warming spices.
Seafood or vegetables lightly coated in a cold batter and quickly deep-fried to a delicate, crisp finish, then served with dipping sauce or salt.
A Japanese breaded and deep-fried pork cutlet sliced into strips and served with tangy tonkatsu sauce, shredded cabbage, and rice.
The Argentine tradition of grilling beef and other meats over wood or charcoal, with slow cooking, simple seasoning, and chimichurri at the table.
An Indonesian chicken rice porridge topped with shredded chicken, scallions, fried shallots, crackers, soy sauce, and sometimes a soft-boiled egg.
A family of stuffed vegetable and vine-leaf dishes filled with rice, herbs, meat, or grains, then simmered or braised in the cuisines of the eastern Mediterranean and Near East.
Japanese pan-fried dumplings with thin wrappers and a filling of pork, cabbage, garlic chives, and ginger, browned on one side and steamed to finish.
Indonesian grilled fish rubbed with a sweet-spicy spice paste, cooked over charcoal, and served with sambal, lime, and rice.
An Indonesian stuffed pancake with savory egg, meat, and scallion fillings or a thick sweet version layered with chocolate, peanuts, cheese, or condensed milk.
A Minangkabau rice meal served with an assortment of rich curries, vegetables, sambal, and meat or fish dishes, named for the city of Padang.
Round Japanese street-food batter cakes cooked in a molded pan around pieces of octopus and topped with sauce, mayonnaise, seaweed, and bonito flakes.
Peruvian skewers, traditionally made with marinated beef heart, grilled over charcoal and served with potatoes, corn, or a bright chili sauce.
A griddled or baked cornmeal cake from northern South America, split and filled or topped with cheese, meat, beans, avocado, or eggs.
A Latin American rice-and-chicken dish in which rice is cooked with sofrito, stock, herbs, and vegetables around browned chicken pieces.
A Levantine dip of fire-roasted eggplant blended with tahini, lemon juice, garlic, and olive oil, often finished with parsley or pomegranate seeds.
A substantial Colombian platter of beans, rice, ground meat, chicharrón, fried egg, plantain, avocado, and arepa associated with the Antioquia region.
Parboiled, dried, and cracked wheat used as a staple grain in pilafs, salads, kibbeh, and stuffed vegetables across the Middle East and Mediterranean.
Cantonese barbecued pork marinated in a glossy blend of maltose or honey, soy, fermented bean curd, and five-spice before being roasted and sliced.
Roasted poblano chiles stuffed with picadillo, covered in a walnut cream sauce, and garnished with pomegranate and parsley in the colors of the Mexican flag.
An Argentine street-food sandwich of grilled chorizo in a crusty roll, usually finished with chimichurri and salsa criolla.
Chinese wheat noodles stir-fried with vegetables and a choice of meat, seafood, or tofu, with regional versions ranging from crisp to soft noodles.
Sichuan noodles dressed with a spicy sesame or peanut sauce, preserved mustard greens, chili oil, Sichuan pepper, scallions, and often minced pork.
A richly spiced Ethiopian chicken stew with onions, berbere, clarified butter, and boiled eggs, traditionally eaten with injera.
Seasoned meat stacked on a vertical spit, slowly roasted and shaved to order, then served in bread or a flatbread with vegetables, herbs, and sauces.
A Levantine bread salad of lettuce and seasonal vegetables tossed with toasted or fried pieces of pita, lemon, olive oil, and sumac.
A Filipino braise of meat, seafood, or vegetables simmered in vinegar, soy sauce, garlic, bay leaf, and black pepper until deeply savory and tender.
A thick Italian flatbread enriched with olive oil, dimpled before baking, and commonly finished with salt, rosemary, olives, tomatoes, or onions.
A Filipino shaved-ice dessert layered with sweet beans, fruit, jellies, leche flan, evaporated milk, and often a scoop of ice cream.
A South American preparation of fresh corn, onion, and spices ground or grated into a savory mixture, wrapped in corn husks, and steamed or baked.
A sour, spongy Ethiopian flatbread made from fermented teff batter and used as both a plate and utensil for stews, vegetables, and meat.
A Filipino peanut-based stew of oxtail, beef, or vegetables thickened with ground peanuts and toasted rice, traditionally served with fermented shrimp paste.
A Levantine preparation of bulgur, minced onions, and finely ground meat, shaped into shells or patties and baked, fried, or served raw depending on the regional style.
Seasoned ground meat shaped into balls, patties, or logs and grilled, fried, or braised across the Middle East, South Asia, Central Asia, and the Mediterranean.
A Sichuan stir-fry of chicken, dried chilies, peanuts, scallions, and a savory-sweet sauce with the characteristic fragrance of Sichuan pepper.
A festive Filipino whole-roasted pig cooked slowly over charcoal until the meat is tender and the skin is deeply crisp, served with liver sauce or vinegar.

A Levantine eggplant dish in which roasted eggplant is cooked with tomatoes, chickpeas, onions, garlic, and warm spices. Unlike the Greek casserole, it is usually served as a vegetable mezze or main dish without béchamel.
A Peruvian-Chinese chifa stir-fry of beef, tomatoes, onions, soy sauce, and cilantro served with rice and french fries.
Small Turkish dumplings filled with seasoned meat, boiled or steamed, and served with garlic yogurt, melted butter, dried mint, and red pepper.
A Turkish breakfast of softly scrambled eggs cooked with tomatoes, green peppers, olive oil, and spices, sometimes enriched with onion, cheese, or sucuk.
A complex Mexican sauce from Puebla combining dried chilies, spices, nuts or seeds, aromatics, and chocolate, traditionally served over turkey or chicken.
A savory Japanese pancake of batter, cabbage, and chosen fillings cooked on a griddle and finished with okonomiyaki sauce, mayonnaise, seaweed, and bonito flakes.
A Beijing preparation of air-dried and roasted duck with lacquered, crisp skin, carved tableside and wrapped in thin pancakes with scallions and sweet bean sauce.
A Turkish boat-shaped flatbread topped with cheese, minced meat, vegetables, or egg and baked in a hot oven until the crust is crisp and the center remains tender.
A family of Indonesian and Southeast Asian chili relishes made by pounding fresh or dried chilies with aromatics, acid, salt, and sometimes shrimp paste or fruit.
Skewers of marinated meat grilled over charcoal and served with a rich peanut sauce, lontong or rice cakes, and fresh pickles across Southeast Asia.
A Filipino sour soup of meat, seafood, or vegetables in a tamarind-based broth with tomatoes, onions, and local greens.
Japanese noodles made primarily from buckwheat flour, served chilled with dipping sauce or hot in a dashi-based broth with seasonal toppings.
A Levantine herb salad built around finely chopped parsley, tomato, mint, onion, and bulgur dressed with lemon juice and olive oil.
Delicate steamed soup dumplings from the Jiangnan region, filled with pork and savory aspic that melts into broth inside the wrapper.
Japanese chicken pieces and offal skewered on bamboo, grilled over charcoal, and seasoned with tare sauce or salt.
A Bursa specialty of sliced döner meat over pieces of pide, covered with tomato sauce and melted butter and served with yogurt on the side.
A Turkish aubergine dish of fried slices in tomato-pepper meat sauce, typically without béchamel and often served with pilav.
